title: Raducanu to return at January's United Cup after injury lay-off
article_text:
Emma Raducanu will make her return to tennis in the United Cup team competition in Australia in the first week of 2027.

Britain's 2021 US Open champion has not played since June because of a stress fracture of the shin.

Raducanu was beaten by Croatia’s Donna Vekic in her first grass-court final at Queen's Club on 14 June, but had to pull out of Wimbledon on the eve of her opening match just 14 days later.

The 23-year-old contemplated playing a couple of events in Asia this autumn but, by delaying her return until January, she will be able to use a special ranking of 38 to enter tournaments.

A special ranking is available to players who have been out with injury for at least six months. In Raducanu's case, it reflects her position in the world rankings after Wimbledon, as she received some prize money despite not playing a match there.

The current British number five will be able to use a special ranking to enter eight events next year, including two Grand Slams and five WTA 1000 tournaments.

Her actual ranking of 107 would likely be too low to make the main draw of January's Australian Open and most other WTA Tour events.

But with a special ranking, Raducanu will not only be assured of playing in Melbourne but also at the WTA 1000 events in Doha, Dubai, Indian Wells and Miami which follow in February and March.

The entry deadline for the United Cup passed on Monday, shortly after Raducanu had her application for a special ranking approved.

A ranking of 38 will make her the British number one for the purposes of this event, giving her the chance to play alongside Arthur Fery in a competition featuring 18 national teams.

Francesca Jones, Jan Choinski and doubles players Neal Skupski and Olivia Nicholls complete the British team for the tournament, which takes place from 1-10 January.

Britain will play Australia and France in their group matches in Sydney, and Raducanu can expect to be face current top-40 players Talia Gibson and Diane Parry.

Raducanu made a gradual return to training in early September - and four months is a long time to train without any competitive action.

She may also not play any exhibitions between now and the end of the year but a spell of warm weather training is anticipated, with the Middle East a popular destination for players in the run-up to the Australian Open.

Recent practice sessions in London with head coach Andrew Richardson and LTA national coach Alex Ward have been increasing in intensity, according to observers.

But by the time Raducanu returns, she will have been on the sidelines for over six months. Playing a few tournaments in Asia would have helped her regain some match sharpness, and perhaps allowed for a faster start to 2027.

Her fellow Briton Sonay Kartal is a fine example, having enjoyed considerable success since returning from six months out with a stress fracture of the back in September.

After reaching the third round of the China Open in her first WTA Tour event back, she beat world number six Elina Svitolina and then world number 12 Belinda Bencic on her way to the Wuhan Open final.

Kartal says there were a "lot of conversations" about where she should make a return.

"I think I wanted to just go straight in. I trusted that I would be able to get my level back, I just didn't know how quickly," the 25-year-old said.

"But I still think there is a long way to go. I can produce the level, but can I sustain it?

"Rehab is draining, and the body is not used to a lot of matches on the tour, so I do feel the aches and the pains from that."

There will only be 24 candles on Raducanu’s birthday cake later this week, but there is no escaping the amount of time she has missed since her stunning New York victory as a teenage qualifier.

She has averaged just 31 matches a season in the five years since that triumph. Players with aspirations to be inside the world's top 20 would hope to play around twice that number.

Elena Rybakina, for example, played 68 matches across 20 tournaments this year as she rose to the top of the world rankings for the first time.

By contrast, Raducanu played just 21 matches, losing in the second round of the Australian Open and the first round at Roland Garros.

Last year, Raducanu contested a career-best 50 matches, and earlier this year rose to 23 in the rankings shortly after reaching the final in the Romanian city of Cluj.

But her early preparation was affected by bone bruising of the foot, and she did not play for two months between March and May because of a post-viral illness picked up in Cluj.

Raducanu said a stress fracture of the shin was only confirmed after a final scan on the night before Wimbledon. But in her desperation to play, she had continued to train at times in the run-up to the championships, when medical advice had suggested that might be unwise.

title: Emma Raducanu's 202-day tennis absence pays off as comeback confirmed
article_text:
Emma Raducanu has finally confirmed her return to competition at the United Cup after spending months sidelined by a shin injury. The 23-year-old will represent Team GB along with British No. 1 Arthur Fery, and they face France and Australia in the group stages at the beginning of January. Raducanu has not played a match since she lost the Queen's final to Donna Vekic in mid-June. She subsequently pulled out of Wimbledon on the eve of the tournament and has given little updates on her comeback since.

But Raducanu's lengthy absence has paid off, as she has spent enough time sidelined by injury to get a protected ranking. This is offered to players who have been out for six months, and is based on their ranking before their absence. It can be used to enter up to eight tournaments, including two Grand Slams.

Raducanu currently sits at No. 107 in the world this week, but entered the United Cup with a protected ranking of No. 38, high enough to get into the main draw of any big tournament. It's likely she will use this to enter the Australian Open.

The former US Open champion will face France's Diane Parry in her comeback match on January 2 - 202 days after she lost in the Queen's final. Britain then takes on Australia on January 3, so Raducanu will be up against Talia Gibson.

As well as Raducanu and Fery, Britain will also be represented by Jan Choinski and Francesca Jones, and doubles stars Neal Skupski and Olivia Nicholls. They will face a strong French team, led by world No. 7 Arthur Fils.

Fils is joined by three top-100 WTA players, Parry, Leolia Jeanjean, and Fiona Ferro. Top-20 ATP doubles star Manuel Guinard and world No. 444 Geoffrey Blancaneaux are also in the squad.

The Australian squad features Rinky Hijikata, who recently stunned Novak Djokovic at the Paris Masters, plus world No. 36 Gibson. Daria Saville is also set to make a comeback at the United Cup after giving birth earlier this year.

Like Raducanu, she's entered using a protected ranking. Alex Bolt and doubles stars Marc Polmans and Ellen Perez are also on the team.

United Cup ties feature two singles matches, one men's and one women's, before a mixed doubles rubber. There are six groups, competing across Sydney and Perth. Team GB is part of Group D, playing in Sydney.

The winners of Group D will play their quarter-final on January 8. But the best runner-up team across the three groups in Sydney also advance to the quarters. All teams then come together in Sydney for the semi-finals and finals.

title: MLB hit a record $2.12B in team sponsorship as deal sizes rose
article_text:
MLB hit a record $2.12B in team sponsorship as deal sizes rose

Major League Baseball's 30 teams earned a record $2.12 billion in sponsorship revenue by the end of the World Series, according to SponsorUnited. That is up 7.3% from a revised 2025 total, while deal volume rose just 1.2%. Deals got larger: the average reached $590,000, up 5.9%, and carried 8.32 assets on average. Financial was the top category at $349 million.

This story was produced through MarketScale. See how Sports & Entertainment teams put it to work with Events & Onsite Capture.

The data comes from Stamford, Connecticut-based SponsorUnited, a global sports and entertainment intelligence platform, which reported that team revenue across the 30 clubs was a record $2.12 billion at the conclusion of the World Series. Revenue rose 7.3% from a revised 2025 total of $1.98 billion, according to Forbes, while deal volume grew 1.2%.

A longer view makes the pattern clearer. Sports Business Journal, which also covered the SponsorUnited report, puts the rise in MLB team sponsorship value at 57% between 2022, when it stood at $1.35 billion, and 2026. Total deals rose 17% over the same span, from 3,195 to 3,732. Value has grown more than three times as fast as deal count. Clubs aren't mainly selling more partnerships. They're selling bigger ones.

Forbes offers one reading of the rise. Maury Brown writes that the average deal size reached $590,000, up 5.9% year over year, as brands continued to invest in more comprehensive partnerships.

Rohan Nagi, SponsorUnited's vice president of strategy and analytics, told Forbes the numbers reflect steady growth in a mature market, roughly in step with U.S. sports overall. He added that much of MLB's major inventory is already committed, and that the next phase of growth will likely hinge on how the league and its teams innovate around the game and the experience of attending it.

All 30 clubs have struck jersey patch deals, with the average deal at $8.6 million, up 1.3% year over year. SponsorUnited estimates three 2026 patch deals, the White Sox with CME Group, the Rays with Webull and the Giants with Airwallex, generated more than $20 million combined.

Put the two growth rates side by side and the source of the gains shows up. The patch, the most visible single asset, is fully sold, and its average price rose only 1.3%. The overall average deal rose 5.9%. That suggests the extra money is coming less from repricing marquee inventory than from packing more assets into each agreement.

Financial was the top sponsorship category at $349 million, up 11.92% year over year, according to Sports Business Journal. Construction and industry grew fastest of the top five, up 13.19% to $115 million. Beverage ($176 million) and auto ($155 million), long fixtures of ballpark signage, were flat. Insurance rose 3.62% to $151 million.

Those dollar figures show how far ahead the leader is. Financial is worth nearly double beverage, the No. 2 category, and it's still growing faster than the market as a whole. The patch list makes the same point: CME Group, Webull and Airwallex all come from finance, trading or fintech.

For marketers at financial or industrial firms, the data indicates their categories added money fastest among the top sponsorship categories, which could make the remaining slots in them more contested at renewal time.

Churn cuts the other way. There were 632 new brand entrants versus 549 brand exits, according to Sports Business Journal. That turnover suggests inventory does come free even in a market Nagi describes as largely committed. It just tends to come back as part of a bigger bundle.

According to Sports Business Journal, the two teams moving to new ballparks posted the fastest sponsorship revenue growth: the Rays rose 33.8% year over year, and the Athletics climbed 19.3%. That fits Nagi's argument that the next round of growth will come from how teams innovate around the game and the experiences built on it.

The Dodgers still grew 14.5%. Last year the club was the first North American pro sports team to top $200 million in yearly sponsorship revenue. The White Sox grew at the same rate, and the Mariners gained 10.2%.

On deal count, the Reds led the majors with 223 deals, ahead of the Yankees at 171, the Padres at 156, the Braves at 155 and the Astros at 151. None of those five clubs appears in the revenue-growth top five. That gap suggests a long roster of partners and fast-growing sponsorship dollars are two separate achievements.

When a club is moving to a new ballpark, ask which assets in the proposal are tied to the current venue and which carry over, and when the new inventory actually goes live.

The 7.3% growth rate rests on a corrected number. SponsorUnited originally reported 2025 team revenue at $2.05 billion, then lowered it to $1.98 billion after what Jared Riegler, the firm's senior marketing manager, told Forbes was its post-season validation process. The record stands either way.

Forbes also runs the adjusted figures back to 2024's $1.86 billion, which produces annual growth of 6.5% and then 7.1% over the two seasons. Two years in a row in that band, read alongside Nagi's description of a mature market, make the case for treating 2026 as steady compounding. A sponsor budget can plan around that kind of growth. It isn't a surge.

A surge is what baseball looked like three seasons ago. Marketing Dive, covering an earlier SponsorUnited report in November 2023, said team sponsorship revenue grew 23% that season to $1.5 billion, even as rule changes shortened games and cut advertising time. The league added 500 new sponsors, and dynamic dugout signage, bought by 67 brands, was the most purchased asset of 2023. Bob Lynch, SponsorUnited's founder and CEO, called that growth "a pretty big outlier, even compared to other professional sports leagues."

title: Changing of the guard for Blitzboks as side targets SVNS three-peat
article_text:
Olympic qualification and backing up their past two seasons of table-topping form will be one of many challenges South Africa’s Blitzboks will face as they commence their final preparations for the 2026-27 SVNS Series opener in Dubai.

Men’s head coach Philip Snyman is set to name his 13-man squad on Friday South African time, having spent the last few weeks with a 38-man extended training squad at the program’s headquarters in Stellenbosch.

After handing six players their debuts in the 2025-26 SVNS Series, Snyman is set to dive back into South Africa’s deep pool of talent, with several key stars set to be unavailable for the opening fortnight of action in Dubai and Cape Town.

Impi Visser, Zander Reynders, Jayden Nell and 2025-26 SVNS Series Dream team inclusion Shilton van Wyk are big losses for the Blitzboks, with all currently recovering from injuries and guaranteed to miss the 2026 leg of the season.

Mfundo Ndhlovu and Donavan Don are also unavailable, having departed the squad to link up with the Stormers and Sharks respectively in their 2026-27 United Rugby Championship campaigns.

However, the Blitzbok head coach has plenty of exciting options at his disposal, having pulled talent from the Junior Springboks, many of whom are fresh off winning the 2026 World Rugby U20 Championship earlier this year.

Combined with exciting up-and-comers from the Varsity Cup and players from URC sides, it gives Snyman plenty of options and directions for his side to continue their winning run.

“With Olympic Games qualification determined by the final placings of the 2027 World Championship tournaments, we will make sure we have our best team ready for those events,” Snyman said in a statement.

“To be able to do that, we will use the first six tournaments of the series to build depth and cover in certain crucial positions.

“Most of our established group of players are fit and ready, apart from the four injured players, while we also invited some very exciting younger talents into camp.

“There are a number of players who played for the Junior Springboks over the last two years, while some standouts in the FNB Varsity Cup were also drafted into this group.

“We also have some loan players from the franchises, such as JC Mars from the DHL Stormers, who are training with us.”

Competition will be tight for spots – with Snyman not only managing the 13-man squad for the SVNS campaign, but a second side that will also take part in Dubai’s Invitational Tournament happening the same weekend.

The tournament will serve as a valuable opportunity for players knocking on the tour to have time in the saddle against quality opposition – while also being ready to slot into the main squad for Cape Town should the Blitzboks’ injury woes continue.

“No one in the contracted group is resting on their laurels,” Snyman added. “The new players are pushing hard for more permanent opportunities and that delivers a very competitive environment.

“We have seen in the past how important that tournament is for our younger group as they also have international teams playing in that tournament, and it also gives them a real feel of tournament play.”

The Blitzboks squad will be named on Friday, with the side departing for Dubai on Monday, 23rd November.

title: DP World Tour Championship: Rory McIlroy boosts Race to Dubai hopes as Joost Luiten grabs shock early lead
article_text:
Rory McIlroy made a strong start to his bid for a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title, as Joost Luiten grabbed a shock early lead at the DP World Tour Championship.

McIlroy, who needs to finish fourth or better to have a chance of surpassing Eugenio Chacarra in the season-long standings and win the Race to Dubai for an eighth time, carded an opening-round 69 at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

The world No 2 mixed five birdies with two bogeys in breezy conditions on the Earth Course, where he missed an eagle opportunity at the par-five last that would have moved him above Chacarra in the projected Race to Dubai standings.

McIlroy sits in tied-third on three under and within two shots of Luiten, the last player in the field and 56th in the season rankings, who jumped top of the leaderboard after a five-under 67.

Jacob Skov Olesen briefly shared the lead but is one behind Luiten on four under, with Victor Perez, Gregorio De Leo, Freddy Schott and Francesco Laporta all two back alongside McIlroy, while Race to Dubai leader Chacarra opened with a level-par 72.

McIlroy can guarantee Race to Dubai victory by winning this event for a fourth time, with The Masters champion making the dream start by rolling in an eight-foot birdie at the first.

He responded to a three-putt par at the second by birdieing the par-three fourth, then bounced back from a sloppy three-putt from 15 feet at the fifth by taking advantage of the par-five seventh.

Chacarra was over-par until his three-birdie run from the seventh, seeing both reach the turn in 34, before McIlroy holed a birdie from the fringe to briefly get within two of the lead.

The leading pair in the Race to Dubai stumbled slightly over the closing stretch, with Chacarra making two bogeys in three holes from the 13th and McIlroy dropping a shot at the par-five 14th after missing the green with his third shot.

McIlroy hit a glorious approach to within 15 feet at the par-five last to leave a late eagle look, which would have seen him leapfrog Chacarra, although he had to settle for a two-putt birdie after leaving his effort short.

Luiten was in the first pair out on the opening morning and raced to the top of the leaderboard with a front-nine 31, then cancelled out back-to-back bogeys from the 11th by birdieing the 13th and 18th to reclaim top spot.

Olesen is also among those looking to secure PGA Tour membership - available to the top 10 eligible players in the Race to Dubai rankings, with the Dane's final-hole birdie getting him within one of Luiten, on a day where only 22 of the 50-man field finished under-par.

McIlroy was among nine players starting the week with a mathematical chance of topping the Race to Dubai rankings, but Jon Rahm and Daniel Hillier - who both carded one-under 71s - the only others to break par on the opening day.

Casey Jarvis, Jayden Schaper and Ryan Fox - who need a victory to have any chance of claiming No 1 - all started the week with a two-over 74, while major winner Aaron Rai struggled to an opening-round 76.

Rory McIlroy, following a three-under 69: "Anything in the 60s today I felt was a good score. And sort of held it together nicely when I needed to. It was nice to finish with a birdie at the last, and obviously in a pretty good position going into the next few days."

Race to Dubai leader Eugenio Chacarra: "I need to do a couple of things better to be able to have a chance on Sunday, and that's what I'm going to focus on. I think if I fix those, a little strategy-wise and I can putt a little better, I think I'm going to have a chance.

Joost Luiten, following his opening-round 67: "A good opening round. Had a great front nine, five under after nine, then you hope you can push on. The wind picked up and I made two annoying bogeys on 11 and 12. I'm quite happy finishing five under."

title: Pepsico’s Lay’s brand in as new Copa Libertadores sponsor
article_text:
South American soccer's governing body CONMEBOL has struck a commercial deal with global food and beverage giant Pepsico.

Through an agreement unveiled yesterday, the Lay's snack foods brand owned by Pepsico, through the Frito-Lay subsidiary, becomes an official sponsor of CONMEBOL's top-tier Copa Libertadores men's club competition.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The deal has been brokered by heavyweight global sports marketing agency IMG, which has a commercial rights deal in place with CONMEBOL – through the FC Diez Media subsidiary – until 2030.

Media reports have suggested that this new CONMEBOL agreement with Pepsico also runs until 2030.

It has been unveiled with the final of this year's Copa Libertadores set to take place on November 28 in Montevideo, Uruguay, between Brazil's Palmeiras, and Estudiantes of Argentina.

Other Libertadores sponsors, meanwhile, include the likes of EA FC, Amstel, Coca-Cola, Hyundai, Mastercard, TCL, and Mapfre.

The existing Coca-Cola deal is likely the reason PepsiCo's Lay's brand has joined up through this new deal.

Alejandro Dominguez, president of CONMEBOL, commented: "This partnership with Lay’s strengthens the global reach of our competitions and allows us to continue bringing South American football closer to its fans around the world."

In terms of recent CONMEBOL activity, the soccer body announced a renewal with Spanish sports rights and production agency Mediapro earlier this month, through 2030.

Through the extended agreement, the company will take responsibility for producing and distributing the international feed for around 700 matches a year, plus the on-site production of every match played in Bolivia.

Lay's, meanwhile, was also a sponsor of men's soccer's 2022 and 2026 FIFA World Cups, with this year's edition having taken place across Mexico, the US, and Canada.

It was also a partner of the 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup in Australia and New Zealand.

title: Basham starts for Wales against All Blacks as Wainwright ruled out
article_text:
Wales number eight Taine Basham will start his first international in four years as he replaces the injured Aaron Wainwright for the Nations Championship match against New Zealand on Saturday.

Basham is part of a back-row reshuffle with James Botham starting instead of fellow Cardiff flanker Alex Mann, and Jac Morgan completing the trio.

Wing Josh Adams, who scored two tries in the 28-21 victory against Japan, is left out in favour of Leicester wing Gabriel Hamer-Webb who wins only his second cap.

Lock Adam Beard comes in for Ben Carter as head coach Steve Tandy makes four starting changes.

Sale prop Tomas Francis has been ruled out for the rest of the campaign by injury with Cardiff tight-head Keiron Assiratti called into the squad.

Back rower Taine Plumtree and props Gareth Thomas and Dillon Lewis are named among the replacements with Rhys Carre not in the match-day 23.

Leicester back rower Wainwright has proved Wales’ most effective forward ball-carrier in recent times.

Basham was recalled to the Wales squad after impressing for Cardiff.

His previous Wales appearance came as a replacement in the 2024 Six Nations against England, while his last international start came in the 2022 tournament against the same opposition.

It is only his second Test start at number eight.

"I'm delighted that Taine gets an opportunity this weekend," said Tandy.

"It's been a while since his last appearance for Wales but he didn't give up and has put in a lot of dedication and hard work to get back.

"The way he's been playing for Cardiff has been great and I'm excited to see him go on Saturday."

Adams, 31, had made only one start for Cardiff before facing Japan where he had a major effect on the game with two tries and a turnover.

"Four Test matches in a row is a pretty big ask for players," said Tandy.

"There will be some players in our squad who will do the four. There's always that plan to rotate, especially in the autumn, whereas in the Six Nations it's a bit more about what the starting team is."

The Wales head coach said Adams had been "outstanding".

"What he brings off the field to the group is massive. Him coming back, having gone back to play for Cardiff the week before, because he wanted that starting berth," added Tandy.

"It's just having an awareness and ultimately creating the opportunity for Josh to have a bit of a break this weekend.

"It'll be good for him to train this week and it's an opportunity to find out about others.

"We feel it's an opportunity for Gabe to come in this weekend."

Hamer-Webb has been in fine form for his club side having scored a hat-trick against Saracens in the Prem.

It will be a second cap for the 26-year-old after he started the Six Nations defeat against Scotland in February where he endured a difficult debut.

"Even on that Monday, when you spoke to Gabe, the awareness was there," said Tandy.

"Some players would probably shy away from what the game was but you didn't even need to go through it with him he knew, exactly what it was and he's aligned to it.

"You look at the way he's gone to Leicester, with guys like Adam Radwan and Ollie Hassell-Collins in fine form, and he's broken into that.

"So I think he deserves this opportunity."

Beard, 30, will win his 69th cap after playing for his French club Montpellier last weekend.

Wales are looking to improve the line-out after losing six on their own throw against Japan.

"He adds massive experience, but also he's done really well in the summer, so we've got that ability to change," said Tandy.

"Ben Carter and Daf Jenkins have been great and Teddy Williams and Seb Davies have been in good form.

Tandy confirmed Beard will return as the line-out leader as they aim to improve.

"There were couple of issues, whether it be a call or a throw," said Tandy.

"There were also couple of really good reads from Japan, who have some 6ft 9in boys.

"Our line-out has been our real shining lights over the last 12 months but you can have a bad day at the office.

"We know we'll have to make it right on the weekend."

Wales have not beaten New Zealand since 1953 with the All Blacks winning the past 34 matches and scoring more than 50 points on their three previous trips to Cardiff.

Dave Rennie’s side resumed their Nations Championship campaign with an impressive 43-21 victory against Scotland in Edinburgh last weekend.

"We're excited for the opportunity we have against New Zealand," said Tandy.

"It was good to get the win last Saturday, but some elements of our execution weren't where we wanted.

"We have to go up another level this weekend and be more ruthless. We have one of the best teams in the world coming.

"We want to be better and put in an 80-minute performance."

Replacements: Elias, G Thomas, D Lewis, Carter, Plumtree, Morgan-Williams, Edwards, Hennessey.

title: When Carlos Alcaraz injured his knee as he takes ‘precautionary’ measures ahead of the ATP Finals
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz is said to be dealing with a knee injury ahead of the ATP Finals, although it is not expected to see him miss out on the year-end tournament.

The Spaniard has already arrived in Turin for the ATP Finals as he prepares to win the tournament for the first time in his career.

Alcaraz has been spotted with a bandage on his knee on the court in Turin, with many fans worrying up his status after an already injury-riddled season.

The Spaniard missed four and a half months of action due to a wrist injury this year and the last thing he needs is more time away from the sport.

However, there has been a positive update on Alcaraz’s injury by a Spanish journalist who tends to be very reliable when it comes to the world No 3.

Alvaro Sanchez took to social media to ease concerns about Alcaraz’s status ahead of the ATP Finals.

“Some of you are asking me about Carlos Alcaraz’s knee, which he trained with a bandage on yesterday in Turin. What I’m being told is that it’s a precautionary measure for a niggle he’s been carrying since the semifinals in Paris,” said Sanchez.

That would imply that Alcaraz tweaked his knee during his semifinal match against Casper Ruud at the Paris Masters, which he won in straight sets 6-4, 6-4.

“As of TODAY, there’s no REAL danger,” said Alcaraz, about the star’s upcoming appearance at the ATP Finas. “That said, with injuries and niggles, you never know, and I think it’s the right call for the TEAM to take these precautions to minimize risks in case anything happens. Stay calm.”

Alcaraz hit the practice court in Turin with Luís Guto Miguel, who is the current junior world No 1.

It was the first stages of Alcaraz looking to win the year-end tournament for the first time in his career. He has made three previous appearances at the tournament, with his best-effort coming in 2025 when he reached the final.

Alcaraz beat the likes of Felix Auger-Aliassime, Taylor Fritz, Alex de Minaur, and Lorenzo Musetti, before losing to Jannik Sinner in the final.

With no Sinner at the tournament this year, Alcaraz will be one of the overwhelming favourites to win the event in 2026.

The ATP Finals takes place between the 15th and the 22nd November.

title: Emma Raducanu’s first opponent of 2027 has now been confirmed
article_text:
Emma Raducanu has enjoyed an injury-riddled 2026, which has seen her play just 21 matches in the last 11 months.

The British star has suffered from a variety of issues, including injury and illness, which has significantly affected what she has been able to achieve on the WTA Tour in 2026.

Raducanu has not played a competitive tennis match since reaching the final of Queen’s in June, after suffering a stress fracture of the shin at the WTA 500 tournament.

However, Raducanu is set to return to action in the 2027 season and her first opponent of the season has already been confirmed.

Raducanu signed up for the United Cup in Australia at the beginning of the year, where she will represent Great Britain alongside Arthur Fery, Neal Skupski, and Olivia Nicholls.

Great Britain have been drawn to play France in their opening match, which will see Raducanu pitted against Diane Parry in a singles match.

The two women have played each other on two occasions previously, with the pair each picking up a victory.

Raducanu won her first match against Parry, which came in a Billie Jean King Cup tie in 2024. The British star’s three-set victory helped Great Britain beat France 3-1.

Parry earned revenge as they met earlier this year in the first round of the Internationaux de Strasbourg, which the Frenchwoman won in straight sets.

The French star currently sits at world No 34 in the WTA Tour rankings, thanks to some standout moments during the 2026 season.

Parry claimed a WTA 125 title at the Clarins Open on home soil in May and she followed it up by claiming her maiden WTA Tour-level trophy at the Monterrey Open in August.

She will provide a tough test for Raducanu, particularly as she will be playing competitively for the first time in six months.

The United Cup is not the only tournament that Raducanu has been confirmed to play either, as she has also signed up to play Queen’s yet again.

In a statement, Raducanu said: “Making the final of the HSBC Championships was a memorable moment in my career. To do so in London with a home crowd behind me and at a special venue like Queens was an incredible experience.

“The atmosphere throughout the week was electric and hopefully we can create even more memorable moments together next summer.”

Raducanu is expected to play the first part of the season under a protected ranking, after missing six months due to injury.

That means she will be able to play the biggest tournaments in the sport, including the Australian Open.

title: McIlroy makes strong start in bid to equal Montgomerie's record
article_text:
Rory McIlroy made a strong start to his bid for a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai title with a three-under-par opening round at the DP World Tour Championship.

The world number two, whose round included five birdies and two bogeys in windy conditions, is two shots behind early leader Joost Luiten.

Spain's Eugenio Chacarra, who leads McIlroy by 533.93 points in the Race to Dubai standings - with 2,000 available to this week's winner - opened with a level-par 72, while third-placed American Patrick Reed struggled during a 75.

"I think it was a pretty fair score," said six-time major winner McIlroy.

"I could probably stand here and argue that I could have been better, but I could probably stand here and argue that I could have been worse as well.

"I hit the ball well for the most part. It's tricky, the wind makes it tricky. The course set-up is a little more difficult than in previous years.

"The greens are not like Yas Links (in Abu Dhabi) last week. They're not absolutely perfect, so you've got to have your patience a little bit on them too. Overall, happy with the score."

Nine players - Chacarra, McIlroy, Reed, Casey Jarvis, Aaron Rai, Jon Rahm, Ryan Fox, Jayden Schaper and Daniel Hillier - can still clinch the Race to Dubai, but only Chacarra and McIlroy can guarantee the season-long accolade with victory at Jumeirah Golf Estates this week.

Northern Ireland's McIlroy, who is aiming to match Scotland's Colin Montgomerie's record of eight season-long crowns, birdied two of his opening four holes before giving a shot back at the fifth.

He birdied the seventh and 11th, and while he took six at the par-five 14th, he finished with a two-putt birdie four to end joint third.

"You can't win it on the first day, but you can certainly lose it," added McIlroy.

"I played nicely, so there was never any threat of me shooting a bad one.

"But it was possible today to go out there and shoot a couple over and feel like you were sort of out of the tournament.

"To get off to a solid start was very important."

Chacarra, who has won three times already this season, finished his front nine with three straight birdies to turn in two-under 34 but dropped shots at 13 and 15 to lie five back of Luiten.

Rahm, who catapulted himself into contention last week in Abu Dhabi, by winning his first tournament since leaving LIV Golf, mixed four birdies and three bogeys in an opening 71 to sit alongside New Zealand's Hillier.

Jarvis (+2), Schaper (+2), Fox (+2), Rai (+4) all have work to do, while England's Tommy Fleetwood also struggled in an opening 76.

Dutchman Luiten, the lowest-ranked player in the field, turned in five under but cancelled two birdies with two bogeys on the back nine to settle for a 67, one clear of Denmark's Jacob Skov Olesen.

title: Training facilities are becoming women’s sports’ next sponsorship engine, Populous report finds
article_text:
Professional women’s sports have entered a new era.

A state-of-the-art training facility is now necessary for franchises to attract the best players and staff and survive in a fiercely competitive landscape. According to a white paper that global design firm Populous and advisory firm Comeback Ventures released Thursday, companies are reimagining what sponsoring these facilities looks like.

For Denver Summit FC in the National Women’s Soccer League, it meant converting their future naming rights with CommonSpirit Health to upfront infrastructure capital. In the Bay Area, the WNBA Golden State Valkyries’ landmark partnership with Sephora went beyond a naming rights deal, fueling athlete-led storytelling and player-designed fashion events. Whether sponsoring a new league such as Unrivaled or investing in a unique opportunity such as the first performance center shared by WNBA and NWSL teams, women’s sports sponsors are leveling up.

The 16-page white paper was produced by Populous, which has worked on several of the facilities used as examples in their findings, in partnership with Comeback Ventures, an advisory firm that provides strategic management services to clients across sports, media and entertainment. Stakeholders providing insights for their findings include Denver Summit, RAJ Sports, Sequel, Unrivaled and Whitecap Sports Group, a sports investment banking firm.

Sponsors in professional women’s sports, according to the report, are finding ways to establish immersive engagement through their partnerships, rather than treating brand exposure as static inventory, signaling new opportunities for teams and their sponsors. This will likely grow as more teams invest in these facilities, which require outstanding capital that can be fueled by these partnerships, and as the women’s sports space continues to grow.

“As more organizations evaluate these investments, there is a growing opportunity to think more expansively about the role these facilities can play, not only in supporting athlete performance, but also in strengthening partnerships, deepening community engagement, and creating long-term business value,” the white paper reads. “When approached strategically, training facilities become year-round engines for partnerships, content, community engagement, and brand storytelling.”

This is mutually beneficial for teams and sponsors, since women’s sports fans tend to be more engaged with the brands sponsoring their favorite players and teams. A report by MarketCast last year found that, for example, 75 percent of NWSL fans are likely to try products from official sponsors compared to MLS fans, and, similarly, 58 percent of WNBA fans are likely to support official league sponsors compared to 45 percent in the NBA.

Legacy sponsorship models tend to be more static.

The white paper argues that these models were developed when broadcast exposure was the dominant form of sports marketing, which means that brands and teams still rely on a set of metrics, including linear television viewership and static logo exposure, that don’t fully encompass the potential value tied to training facilities. The unique behavior of women’s sports audiences (younger, more digitally native, more values-driven, more engaged with players) is shifting how brands evaluate these partnerships, turning facilities into an opportunity to generate value beyond broadcast.

A facility, the white paper states, offers a daily environment for athletes and staff, production hubs for digital and social content, locations for youth development and mentorship and a year-round destination for fans and local communities — in other words, more touchpoints for brands to engage with athletes and fans.

According to the white paper, the Golden State Valkyries have developed “one of the most deliberate partnership strategies in women’s sports.” One clear example is when Sephora U.S. became the naming rights partner for the 2026 WNBA Champions’ 31,800-square-foot performance center in Oakland and the presenting partner for the “Valkyries Content Day and Training Camp.”

The partnership included game-day activations and non-game-day experiences, including a fashion show featuring player-designed collections and athletes as models. The training facility has become a year-round destination for content, community engagement and brand storytelling, creating a “more durable value” for the team and its partners. This approach resonated commercially, the report argues, and the team’s wild commercial success over the past two years is proof.

The team became the fastest franchise in WNBA history to win a title and the first franchise in women’s professional sports to surpass $100 million in annual revenue in its second season. Recent estimates value the team between $850 million (Sportico) and $1 billion (CNBC), making them possibly the first billion-dollar professional women’s sports team.

Another successful sponsorship model the report points to is Denver Summit FC’s partnership with CommonSpirit Health, which helped finance the team’s training facility. A training facility and access to an elite stadium have become a prerequisite for the NWSL when awarding franchise rights to expansion teams.

“Increasingly, there is more movement in women’s sports to invest in health science and performance, which upped the ante to be a part of what we are doing,” Denver’s president Jen Millet said in the report. “The investment by CommonSpirit is on par with investments across sports, both men’s and women’s. CommonSpirit saw value in being part of the project from the beginning.”

In this case, the club secured CommonSpirit as a founding partner and naming-rights sponsor for their performance center, and then used their long-term contracted sponsorship payments as collateral for a loan to support construction.

A training facility bolsters player recruitment and was surely a driver in helping Denver Summit field its inaugural team for the 2026 season, which included a marquee signing: U.S. women’s national team captain Lindsey Heaps. Guaranteed facilities were an especially important recruitment tool for expansion clubs this year, as the league eliminated its expansion draft.

title: England v Japan: Henry Pollock, Max Ojomoh and Will Joseph start
article_text:
Free-scoring back row Henry Pollock will make only his second start for England after being named at number eight in a much-changed side for Saturday's Nations Championship meeting with Japan.

Despite mainly being restricted to the bench, Pollock has scored eight tries in 14 Tests, including a double as a stand-in wing against Australia on Sunday.

After man-of-the-match performances in Northampton's run to the Prem title, the 21-year-old will get a chance to press his claim to a Test starting spot.

Elsewhere in-form Will Joseph, whose only previous England cap came under now-Japan coach Eddie Jones in 2022, is given his chance in the absence of injured wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso.

Max Ojomoh comes in at inside centre in a remarkable return to favour.

The 26-year-old has not played for England since starring in the win over Argentina a year ago and was not initially part of England's 36-strong squad for this month's matches.

With his contract at Bath up for renewal at the end of the season, he has been linked with a move to the Top 14 in the French press.

However, a stellar performance in England A's win over an Argentina XV last Friday has earned Ojomoh promotion into the senior starting line-up ahead of Fraser Dingwall, with first choice Seb Atkinson ruled out with a hip injury.

George Ford is named at fly-half with Fin Smith, who recovered from a calf injury to play 80 minutes against the Wallabies, rotated out of the matchday squad and Marcus Smith, who has impressed in recent weeks with Harlequins, on the bench.

Cadan Murley comes into the back three with Tommy Freeman left out, while there is an all-new starting front row of Ellis Genge, Luke Cowan-Dickie and Asher Opoku-Fordjour.

Northampton scrum-half Archie McParland is poised to make his debut off the bench, with Greg Fisilau, Arthur Clark and Emmanuel Iyogun, who all have one cap, alongside him in an inexperienced set of replacements.

Enforced absences have prevented England from building on last weekend's win with a similar selection.

Only centre Henry Slade, scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet and captain Maro Itoje have retained their starting spot in the same position.

The rejig, however, gives others a chance to make their case a year out from the Rugby World Cup in Australia.

While Pollock has made regular try-scoring second-half cameos in his England career so far, the 21-year-old's only previous start was in February's dismal 42-21 home defeat by Ireland.

England were routed at the breakdown that day and Pollock's challenge, albeit against weaker opposition, will be to prove his effectiveness in close quarters, as well as in open spaces.

Pollock had Ben Earl and Tom Curry alongside him against Ireland, and Borthwick has brought more ballast into the back-row blend on this occasion with Alex Coles moved to blind-side flanker in place of the injured Ollie Chessum.

Like Pollock, Ojomoh knows that head coach Steve Borthwick will be focused on small details, as much as showreel highlights.

The Bath star's silky playmaking skills and running threat have never been in doubt, but England have wanted more from the Bath star in defence and his work off the ball.

However, if, as expected, England secure the majority of possession, Ojomoh's ability to pick passes in the face of a defence could spring his backline.

Joseph, whose older brother Jonathan won 54 caps for England between 2012 and 2020, has been one of the stars of Gloucester's resurgence this season, alternating between wing and midfield.

England have won all six previous Tests against Japan, most recently running out 52-17 winners in Tokyo in June 2024.

Joseph was taken on England's 2022 tour of Australia by Jones as a teenage apprentice player, alongside fellow London Irish academy product Henry Arundell.

While Arundell's try-scoring cameo in the first Test captured most of the attention, Joseph also made his international bow, coming on for the final minute of the team's second-Test win in place of Guy Porter.

Now 24, it has been a long wait for his next piece of international experience.

"Being back here is quite strange, it feels a little deja-vu," Joseph told Rugby Union Weekly last month about his return to the England camp.

"I feel a lot like a new player, even though I have been here before and know a lot of the lads, but I am just really excited to showcase what I can do."

Since making his last England appearance Joseph has lost the hearing in his left ear as a result of an auto-immune disease.

"I was in a training session, the whistle went and my ear felt a bit funny," he remembered.

"Then we had a swimming session and when I got out the pool I couldn't hear out of my left ear.

"My understanding is that my body over-reacted to something that was going on in my ear and shut down the nerves that allow me to hear. It was scary. It was tough.

"When you have only got one ear [that works] your surroundings are all off. I feel like I have adapted now and got used to playing with one ear, but at the start I wasn't sure whether I was going to be able to do it."

title: 2027 Six Nations format confirmed as Youngs urges change
article_text:
The 2027 Six Nations will stick with its new six-week schedule, but England legend Ben Youngs believes organisers should go even further.

The championship introduced a major scheduling change in 2026, cutting one of its traditional two rest weekends.

That format is set to stay for 2027. Teams will play three rounds in a row before taking a weekend off ahead of the final two matches.

But Youngs isn't convinced the competition needs a break at all.

The former England scrum-half, who won a record 127 caps for his country, has reportedly called for all five rounds to be played on consecutive weekends.

He said: "The Six Nations shouldn't drag on for eight weeks. Let's trim it down to five, pack it with action, and give players a breather afterwards," he declared.

"With a tighter schedule, you'd see better ratings and a lot more nail-biting drama."

That would see the entire championship wrapped up in just five weeks, with no rest weekends between matches.

It's a bold suggestion, particularly given the physical demands of international rugby.

But with the Six Nations already moving away from its traditional schedule, Youngs clearly believes there's room to go one step further.

For more than two decades, the championship was played across seven weeks, with two rest weekends separating the five rounds.

That changed in 2026, partly to accommodate the expanded international calendar and the introduction of the Nations Championship.

The new format offers greater continuity, keeping supporters engaged without lengthy gaps between matches.

However, the reduced recovery time has also raised concerns about player welfare.

Former Wales fly-half Dan Biggar previously warned that consecutive Test matches place enormous physical and mental demands on players.

Speaking about the changes, Biggar explained that rest weekends provided valuable recovery time and allowed coaches to work with their squads.

The debate is particularly relevant ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.

For now, organisers are sticking with one rest weekend.

The championship begins on Friday, 5 February, when Ireland host England at the Aviva Stadium.

Steve Borthwick's side then face defending champions France at Twickenham on Valentine's Day.

England host Italy in round three before travelling to Cardiff to face Wales.

Their campaign concludes against Scotland on Super Saturday, with the Calcutta Cup up for grabs.

France, meanwhile, will be chasing a third consecutive Six Nations title following their dramatic 2026 triumph.

Could the Six Nations scrap rest weekends entirely?

Youngs' reported suggestion would take the championship into new territory.

Five consecutive weekends would create an uninterrupted run of international rugby, potentially increasing interest throughout February and March.

But it would also leave players with even less recovery time during one of the most physically demanding tournaments in the sport.

With no further changes confirmed, the 2027 Six Nations will retain its six-week schedule.

Whether organisers eventually go further remains to be seen.

title: An Se-young, another historic achievement overshadowed by her 55-match winning streak... She has won all 22 matches that reached a 1-1 tie, with foreign media also taking note of the "Queen" 's incredible concentration
article_text:

An Se-young (24, Samsung Life), the "Queen" of Korean badminton, has won the final game in all 22 recent matches where she traded one game each with her opponents. Foreign media have also taken note of An's concentration, which is displayed when the match is tied at 1-1.

Badminton specialist outlet Badminton Planet assessed on the 10th (Korean time), "An Se-young's consistency has been particularly impressive in matches that went to three games." The outlet cited the women's singles final of the 2026 World Badminton Federation (BWF) World Tour Korea Open (Super 500), held on the 8th at Yeosu Jinnam Gymnasium, as an example.

At the time, world No. 1 An Se-young defeated No. 2 Akane Yamaguchi (Japan) 2-1 (21-12, 15-21, 21-16). After winning the first game by a nine-point margin, An fell behind 0-4 from the start of the second game and ultimately lost it 15-21.

It was a moment when she could have easily ceded momentum to Yamaguchi. However, as the match returned to a tie, An rallied again. After pulling ahead 6-1 in the early stages of the third game, she was chased to 11-9 but widened the gap again to secure the championship.

The outlet reported, "Since it was Yamaguchi who handed An Se-young her defeat in last year's final at this tournament, this final carried even greater significance. This time, An emerged victorious after a close battle spanning three games."

It further pointed out, "An Se-young has won all 22 matches that went to three games since losing to Yamaguchi at the 2024 BWF World Tour Finals."

The player who last handed An Se-young a defeat in a three-game match was indeed Yamaguchi. In the group stage of the BWF World Tour Finals held in Hangzhou, China, in December 2024, An lost to Yamaguchi 1-2.

Since then, An began her winning streak in three-game matches by defeating Gao Fangjie (China) 2-1 in the semifinals of the Orleans Masters last March. She also defeated Yamaguchi 2-1 in the women's team semifinal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games last September.

Her three most recent titles were also hard-fought battles that went to three games. In the Denmark Open final last month, An faced Yamaguchi again and lost the first game 21-23 after a deuce. However, she took the next two games 21-14 and 21-18 to secure a comeback victory.

An also achieved a comeback win in the French Open final. After losing the first game 16-21 to India's star player Pusarla V. Sindhu, she took the second game 21-11. In the final game, she allowed only 12 points to Sindhu to claim the top spot.

The stage where An completed her 22-match winning streak was this Korea Open final. The outlet assessed, "It was a match that showed how An Se-young regains momentum," adding, "Although she lost the second game, she took the final game against one of the top contenders in women's singles."

An Se-young herself cited mental strength as a changed aspect. According to reports, after finishing the Korea Open final, An reflected that she had become mentally stronger than last year and had learned how to change the flow of the game even when her energy was nearly depleted during play.

The outlet explained, "This growth has contributed to her rarely showing fluctuating performance while handling a tight international tournament schedule."

An Se-young's record this season is 71 wins and 1 loss, with a winning percentage of 98.6%. Her only defeat was against Wang Zhiyi (China) in the All England Open final last March. Since then, An has won 55 consecutive matches and lifted her 11th championship trophy of the season at the Korea Open.

An Se-young has won eight times on this year's World Tour and also claimed titles at the Asian Championships, World Championships, and Asian Games. Following last year, she is again on par with Japan's men's singles player Kento Momota, who set the record for the most singles titles in a single season in 2019. An Se-young is the first singles player to win 11 times in two consecutive seasons.

After a brief rest, An Se-young will challenge for her 12th title of the season at the BWF World Tour Finals to be held in Hangzhou, China, in December. She is also aiming to surpass the women's singles longest winning streak record (59 consecutive wins) set by Indonesia's legend Susi Susanti.

Badminton Planet stated, "An Se-young's 'normal performance,' having lost only once in 72 matches, is at a level that opponents find difficult to match," adding, "An Se-young still has the opportunity to make her already historic year even more special."

title: Fortescue Zero grows Formula E presence with Jaguar partnership
article_text:
Jaguar TCS Racing, the Formula E all-electric motor racing team, has announced a new multi-year partnership with Fortescue Zero, the green energy tech arm of Australian metals and mining giant Fortescue.

Through the deal, Elysia, Fortescue Zero’s electric battery brand, will become the official battery intelligence partner of Jaguar TCS Racing, supporting the team’s overhaul into the new generation of technical regulations, termed ‘Gen4’.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The team's parent company Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) already leveraged Elysia tech for the development of its own consumer electric vehicles, an agreement in place since 2024.

Now, Fortescue Zero will collaborate with the team to support the development of new battery products going forward across the multi-season agreement.

Speaking on the deal, Jaguar TCS Racing team principal Ian Jame commented: “Technical innovation will be critical to success in this new chapter of Formula E, and what makes this partnership particularly exciting is the opportunity to demonstrate how innovation developed through the demands of motorsport can drive meaningful benefits beyond the race track.”

The Elysia brand will feature on the nose cone of the Jaguar racing cars throughout the agreement. This season those cars will be driven by former Formula 1 racer Stoffel Vandoorne of Belgium, who won the Formula E driver’s championship in 2021-22, and Portugal’s António Félix da Costa, who won two ePrix races for Jaguar in 2025-26.

Jaguar TCS Racing is perhaps the most successful team of the Formula E ‘Gen3’ era, having finished no lower than second in the team standings since the Gen3 regulations were introduced ahead of the 2022-23 campaign.

Indeed, the team won the teams championship in the 2023-24 season, and again in the 2025-26 campaign, making them the current defending world champions.

Other prominent sponsors this season include naming rights partner Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), oil company Castrol, Dow Mobility Science, financial services firm Chase Bank, and, of course, team owner Jaguar, the iconic luxury car brand of JLR.

The 2026-27 Formula E campaign will begin with the two-round Jeddah ePrix in Saudi Arabia on December 18 and 19, 2026, and run through the two-round Tokyo ePrix in Japan on July 24 and 25, 2027.

For its part, this is not Fortescue’s first foray into motorsport, or even Formula E.

Indeed, since 2024, Fortescue has been the official pit boost supplier of Formula E, utilizing its tech advancements to aid on-track action across the series.

Back in January 2022, the firm acquired Williams Advanced Engineering (WAE), the advanced technology and engineering arm of the Williams Racing team, of the prestigious Formula 1 motor racing series.

That deal served as a means of gaining access to WAE’s battery technology, which has been partly developed on the track with Williams, illustrating its investment in the electric powertrain industry and, as such, its grounding for a Formula E team.

Most recently, Fortescue Zero entered the series proper as a competitor, acquiring the Penske Autosport team.

title: ATP Tour announces record growth, partnership revenues surpass $100m
article_text:
The ATP Tour, the top-tier men’s tennis tour, has announced record commercial partnership revenues this year of over $100 million after securing a slate of major sponsorship agreements.

The tour announced today that its central partnership revenues had increased 49% year-on-year in 2026 to more than $100 million for the first time on the back of new agreements and expanded investments from long-standing partners including flag carrier airline Emirates, tech company Infosys, parts manufacturer Nitto, luxury carmaker Lexus, home appliances corporation Haier, and tyre manufacturer Yokohama.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The figure, which represents an increase of more than 200% since 2022, has also been driven by new partnerships with global investment organization EQT and US tennis brand K-Swiss, while the ATP also announced a new multi-year partnership with Julius Baer earlier this week, with the firm serving as the tour’s first wealth management partner.

The organization also renewed its partnership with video streaming technology firm Deltatre, covering graphics, data, and production across the 2026 season, and expanded its behind-the-scenes content partnership with Overtime, the youth-focused US sports media company, to boost its younger fanbase.

The ATP also announced global content partnerships with TikTok and Spotify, as well as launching global marketing campaigns and a new brand identity.

Daniele Sano, ATP chief business officer, said: “Since 2022, we have more than tripled our partnership revenues through a combination of new agreements and increased investment from longstanding partners.

“This success is providing benefits across the tour. Many of our central partnerships include on-site rights at ATP tournaments, and more than 70% of partnership revenues are paid to tournaments for the rights and activation they provide to our partners.

“Our new partnership with Julius Baer adds further momentum, and we remain confident in our outlook as we target a further double-digit increase in partnership revenues in 2027.”

The increase comes almost four years after the ATP Tour’s chairman, Andrea Gaudenzi, launched OneVision, the organization's long-term strategic plan to reform professional tennis, align interests between players and tournaments, and grow the sport’s commercial digital footprint.

Earlier this year, the tour re-elected Gaudenzi as chairman for a third term until 2028.

The ATP said improved tournament infrastructure and growing audiences across its digital and social platforms have increased the value of the tour’s partnerships, while its global footprint allows brands to scale partnerships across multiple markets and tailor activations to specific markets and audiences.

Growth has also been driven by the launch of the ATP’s dedicated Licensing and Retail team within its central business division in 2025, which has opened the door to new licensing agreements, including K-Swiss’ agreement to create a collection of five ATP-branded tennis shoes.

title: T-Mobile Powers New Ways to Experience the FORMULA 1 HEINEKEN LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX On and Off the Track
article_text:
BELLEVUE, Wash.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov. 12, 2026--

T-Mobile (NASDAQ: TMUS) is bringing its Formula 1 regional partnership to life at the intersection of performance and culture. At one of the world’s most exciting and demanding live events, the network helps the race run smarter and gives fans and members more ways to experience it.

Those same demands make the Las Vegas Grand Prix a proving ground, giving T-Mobile a place to put America’s most advanced 5G network to work, test new capabilities at scale and help shape how connectivity powers the next generation of live experiences.

“F1 in Vegas is where performance becomes culture. Everything is happening at full speed, on and off the track, with fans tuned in from around the world,” said Lucy McLellan, Executive Vice President and Chief Brand & Communications Officer at T-Mobile. “This is exactly the kind of environment where we can put our network to work at scale and see that impact carry through the entire experience, from how the race runs and how fans experience it to how we put our members inside the action. We’re in T-Mobile’s next era of disruption, with a network capable of doing things we wouldn’t have imagined even a year ago. Formula 1 is exactly the kind of partner that keeps us pushing further.”

See the Race from New Angles. Fans watching around the world will get sweeping new views from across the track and T-Mobile Zone at Sphere, bringing them deeper into the race.T-Mobile will support with more than 20 5G-connected devices, including drones and roaming cameras, using 5G on Demand and network slicing fromT-Mobile Advanced Network Solutions (ANS). The ANS setup can reach places traditional cables and production trucks can’t easily go, bringing viewers a part of the action that would otherwise be difficult to capture with traditional wired production.

A Smarter Command Center Keeps Race Weekend Moving. T-Mobile will power and operate an evolved Smart Operations Command Center that brings crowd density and flow data, food and beverage line management and transportation tracking into a single real-time 3D view of the track so event organizers can spot and stay ahead of issues, ease bottlenecks and support safer operations for fans and staff.

More Race Weekend, Less Time in Line. The T-Mobile network helps keep things moving with connectivity for more than 500 ticket scanners and point-of-sale devices, SuperMobile for LasVegas Grand Prix staff and T-Priority for first responders, giving them dedicated connectivity when the event is at its busiest.

T-Mobile approaches sponsorships differently. Since the inaugural race in 2023, T-Mobile has worked side by side with Las Vegas Grand Prix as an operational technology partner, going beyond logo placement to play a more active role in testing new capabilities and experiences in one of the world’s most demanding live environments.

“We built America’s best network to connect people, but that’s not the whole story. What we’re building now is the foundation to bring an intelligent world to life,” said John Saw, President of Technology and Chief Technology Officer, T-Mobile. “That requires a network that can close the distance between data and decision, instantly, reliably, at scale. Vegas gives us the environment to prove it. As the leader in 5G, we’re already putting the network to work in new ways, and as we look toward the next generation of wireless connectivity, we’re using that lead to drive what comes next.”

T-Mobile’s approach includes providing a 5G private network and network slicing for broadcast production, a Smart Operations Command Center for smarter, faster and more informed decision making, and real-time connectivity through T-Priority and mission critical push to talk solutions. What T-Mobile learns here can help shape smarter, more responsive network capabilities for business customers and consumers alike, while supporting critical connectivity for first responders.

Race week in Las Vegas is unlike any other event on the sports calendar — and T-Mobile members get more of it. From an exclusive moment with Lando Norris before the racing starts to front-row views of the track and T-Mobile Stage from Club Magenta, T-Mobile is making sure members are at the center of everything race week has to offer.

The T-Mobile Stage Goes Live to the World. For the first time, fans virtually anywhere can watch three nights ofT-Mobile Stage performances live on the F1 YouTube channel. Up to 20 5G-connected cameras will give viewers a front-row seat to the stage and crowd in 4K, with select fan footage feeding directly into F1’s event broadcast. The stage lineup includes:

title: Full-back Barrett leads New Zealand for first time
article_text:
Full-back Beauden Barrett will captain New Zealand for the first time when he leads out the All Blacks for the Nations Championship game against Wales in Cardiff on Saturday.

All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has made eight starting changes from the side that defeated Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield with 10 alterations in the match-day 23.

It will be 35-year-old Barrett's first time as starting skipper in his 149th international with brother Scott also named at lock, while Richie Mo'unga is at fly-half.

"Beauden brings such valuable experience and is massively respected by us all," said Rennie.

"Captaining the All Blacks in a Test is an honour I know he doesn't take lightly, so it'll be a proud day for him and his whanau [family]."

The All Blacks defeated Scotland 43-21 last Saturday, but record try-scoring wing Will Jordan (hamstring) and centre Jordie Barratt (facial) picked up injuries and are absent against Wales.

Flanker Anton Segner and wing Fehi Fineanganofo, whose move to Newcastle Red Bulls in the summer was delayed by a year, make their first Test starts.

Segner, prop George Bower, hooker Asafo Aumua and scrum-half Cortez Ratima move from the replacements into the starting side.

Mo'unga, Fineanganofo, lock Josh Lord and centre Anton Lienert-Brown also come into the side.

"We have created good depth in this group and there is a lot of competition for places," said Rennie.

"We have selected a strong squad with 783 caps."

New Zealand have won the past 34 Tests against Wales in a winning sequence that stretches back to 1953.

"Wales are a proud rugby nation and building nicely under Steve Tandy," said Rennie.

"We are well aware of the threat they pose and the challenge of playing in front of a passionate crowd at Principality Stadium."

New Zealand and South African are currently unbeaten in the southern hemisphere table.

The rivals are battling for top spot before the play-off weekend at the end of the month.

New Zealand: B Barrett (capt); Fineanganofo, Tupaea, Lienert-Brown, Moorby; Mo'unga, Ratima; Bower, Aumua, Newell, S Barrett, Lord, Segner, Lakai, Sititi.

Replacements: Bell, Numia, Tosi, Hannah, E Blackadder, Fainga'anuku, Preston, R Ioane.

title: England's Mitchell could miss Six Nations after hamstring operation
article_text:
England scrum-half Alex Mitchell could miss next year's Six Nations after an operation to fix recurring hamstring issues.

The 29-year-old, who was Steve Borthwick's first-choice nine last season, has gone under the knife after suffering four hamstring injuries this year.

If Mitchell, who has recovered ahead of schedule in the past, follows an estimated four-month rehabilitation it would give him a chance of playing in England's final two matches, against Wales and Scotland on 6 and 13 March.

Any setback however would leave him with only pre-tournament friendlies to play in for England before next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia.

Mitchell's latest hamstring injury, which came in Northampton's win over Gloucester last month, ruled him out of this month's Nations Championship campaign.

Mitchell suffered an injury to the same hamstring against Ireland in February and again against Fiji in July. He also tweaked his other hamstring - his left, non-kicking leg - in an England training camp in May.

Mitchell told the i Paper last month, external that he had been given the option, like skipper Maro Itoje, to skip England's summer fixtures against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina, but opted to play instead.

While Jack van Poortvliet has emerged as Borthwick's starting pick in Mitchell's absence, there is competition behind the Leicester man with Bristol's Harry Randall, Bath's Ben Spencer and Mitchell's club team-mate Archie McParland all vying for position.

Mitchell travelled to Finland to be operated on by Lasse Lempainen, a specialist in elite sporting injuries.

Chelsea and England defender Reece James and Paris St-Germain's Ballon D'Or winner Ousmane Dembele are among Lempainen's previous patients, both returning to consistent playing time after a string of muscular injuries.

Mitchell's England team-mate Ben Curry was also operated on by Lempainen and has made a successful return to action after 10 months out, featuring in England's win over Australia last weekend.

Curry posted "hamstring final boss" beneath an Instagram post marking Mitchell's operation., external

title: Svitolina stays in WTA Finals hunt after remarkable fightback sees off Muchova
article_text:
Elina Svitolina staged a remarkable comeback to beat Karolina Muchova and remain in the hunt for the WTA Finals title.

The Ukrainian appeared to be on her way out of Indian Wells when she was a set down and required an eight-minute medical timeout. But she recovered to win 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 and stay in with a chance of reaching the semi-finals.

Svitolina, who was demolished 6-4, 6-0 by Mirra Andreeva in her opening round-robin match, told Sky Sports: “It was not an easy task to do.

“I was pretty angry at myself after the first match and after the first set also. Things didn’t go my way, so I tried to direct this anger towards the ball and found my game in the end.

“I think the level was back in the third set. I just tried to give it all in this match because I know I would be eliminated if I lost. So I just tried to really release all this energy and find these openings against Karolina. She’s such a tough opponent.

“It’s the last tournament of the season, so I just have to really put my head down and deal with all the small injuries.

“I mean, it’s normal that everyone is tired. Everyone is struggling with something here and there. I will just try to do my best, have an ice bath and try to heal as much as possible in the next 48 hours.”

Svitolina faces a straight shootout with Aryna Sabalenka for second place in the group. Andreeva, the French Open champion, secured her place in the last four after coming from 4-1 down in the first set to beat Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0.

Andreeva tops Group B with Sabalenka second and Svitolina third.
