title: LPGA to update pace-of-play policy with stricter punishments
article_text:
The LPGA is updating its pace-of-play policy and dishing out stricter punishments in 2027 after pace flatlined during the 2026 season.

Players were informed of the changes by the Pace of Play Committee during a Tuesday meeting at The Annika in Belleair, Florida, the LPGA’s penultimate event of the season.

The updated policy will include more fines.

Previously, players who took one to five seconds over their allotted time to hit a shot were given two warnings before a fine. Now the warnings are gone and players will be fined right away. Six to 15 seconds over allotment remains a one-stroke penalty but a fine will now be included, and 16 seconds or more remains a two-stroke penalty but will also come with a fine.

The LPGA has tracked data since the new policy went into place in 2025 and came away with three main findings: that pace of play improved in 2025 but recently flatlined; warnings and penalties increased; and the number of holes timed increased by 12 percent.

Under the previous policy, there were three one-stroke penalties and two two-stroke penalties in 2025, and this year there have been five one-stroke penalties and two two-stroke penalties. Recently, Carlota Ciganda and Yealimi Noh were each handed two-stroke penalties for slow play at the Buick LPGA Shanghai last month.

Nelly Korda and Charley Hull, two of the LPGA’s most popular (and fastest) players, were asked about the policy at The Annika on Wednesday. Both were in favor of the changes.

“I’m a big fan,” Korda said. “Anything to get the game a little faster for us players, for fans, for everyone, I think they’re doing a really good job. I mean, at the end of the day, no one wants to be out here for five-plus hours. No player wants to. Nobody wants to watch it. I think we’re just moving in the right direction.”

Beyond the fines that will be introduced in 2027, two other changes were also announced: A player who reaches 35 timed holes will be fined (down from 40); and the time allowed for a shot has been decreased from 70 seconds to 60 seconds.

“Pace of play matters to our players, our fans and our partners, and we committed to reviewing our policy every year to make sure it’s working,” an LPGA spokesperson told GOLF. “After a close look at this season’s data and conversations with our players, we’re strengthening the policy for 2027 with tighter time limits and stronger, earlier consequences for players who exceed them. Going forward, we’ll keep measuring, keep listening to our players and keep adjusting as we work to further improve pace of play.”

After this week’s Annika, the LPGA season concludes next week with the season-ending CME Group Tour Championship at Tiburon Golf Club in Naples.

title: LIV Golf is dead, but its remnants are already all over the tour it tried to 'destroy'
article_text:
LIV Golf is dead. The time of death for the rebel league came last week in a bankruptcy hearing, when LIV’s lawyers informed the court they would begin winding down toward liquidation and that LIV Golf 2.0 would not go forward as they hoped.

While the former Saudi-backed league will soon fade into golf history, the remnants of it are all over the tour it tried “to destroy.”

“They took players, they took sponsors, they turned professional golf into an arms race,” Rory McIlroy said last week in Abu Dhabi about LIV’s threat to the DP World Tour. “They were going around Augusta saying they wanted to destroy the European Tour.”

That goal failed, and now LIV’s former standard bearers will populate its former target. At this week’s DP World Tour Championship, eight former LIV golfers will tee it up. Two of them (Eugenio Chacarra and Bernd Wiesberger) left LIV while it was still burning through cash. Patrick Reed abandoned ship in January in an attempt to earn his PGA Tour card through the European circuit, which he did quite easily. The others, including Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton, recently said goodbye to LIV as it entered bankruptcy and tried to sway them to buy into LIV 2.0.

This week in Dubai, three of LIV’s previous trophy defections have a chance to claim the DP World Tour’s Race to Dubai title. Chacarra, who might be the biggest winner of golf’s civil war, has won three times this year and enters the final event atop the standings. Reed, who was among the initial wave of defections, has won twice and is third behind Chacarra and Rory McIlroy. Then there’s Rahm, who won last week in his first start post-LIV to vault up the standings, giving himself a chance to win this week and take the top prize.

LIV’s tentacles will be all over the DP World Tour next year as players who left LIV use it to make their way back to the PGA Tour, which has not yet decided on a path back for defectors. McIlroy believes that having LIV’s top players battle for a handful of tickets to the PGA Tour’s Championship Series will be a massive boon to the European circuit.

“It would be an amazing thing for this tour if all those guys were funneled through the DP World Tour and were made to qualify that way,” McIlroy told reporters last week in Abu Dhabi. “I think that’s the right scenario and the right decision and also makes this tour incredibly strong.

“It’s only going to be into the Championship Series. It’s only going to be a handful of cards so it’s going to be very, very competitive.”

Reed and Chacarra will head to the PGA Tour next year, but both have said they plan to play on the DP World Tour as well. Rahm, Hatton, David Puig, Adrian Meronk, Laurie Canter, Victor Perez, Tom McKibbin and Thomas Detry have DP World Tour status for next season. Sergio Garcia announced his plans to return to the DP World Tour after his LIV exit and can take up membership through the Legends career money exemption. Lee Westwood, Ian Poulter, Martin Kaymer, Graeme McDowell, Paul Casey, Louis Oosthuizen and Branden Grace can also join through that category if they want. Dustin Johnson and Joaquin Niemann could accept tournament invites under a new policy that will grant spots to top players left in limbo after LIV’s collapse.

“Until I get clarity on [my PGA Tour status], my plan would be to spend the year on the DP World Tour, and I’m looking forward to it,” Rahm said last week in Abu Dhabi. “Currently looking at the schedule to see how I can organize to play the events I want to play. You know, maybe have a chance to have a bit of a different year to what I have in the past.”

Three former LIV players earned their 2027 DP World Tour cards on Wednesday via DP World Tour Q School. Josele Ballester was co-medalist, while Byeong Hun-An and John Catlin also finished inside the top 15.

Then, there’s the question of Bryson DeChambeau.

LIV’s biggest champion released a statement on Sunday about the end of the league and said he’d approach whatever comes next with “humility.” The DP World Tour can offer DeChambeau membership by virtue of his 2024 U.S. Open win, but he has to commit by next week. McIlroy has admitted he’s not a “fan” of DeChambeau but knows having him in fields would be good for the DP World Tour’s health.

“I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments,” McIlroy said Tuesday in Dubai. “And honestly, look, I’m certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be, but it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options. You know, if he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options.”

LIV Golf is deceased. But what’s left of it is already taking over the DP World Tour. That’ll be evident this week in Dubai, where three defectors have a legitimate chance to win the tour’s season-long crown. It will be even more apparent next season, when typically sleepy DP World Tour fields are expected to be littered with past major champions and former LIV stars who will at least temporarily call the European circuit home.

title: Svitolina comes back from a set down to beat Muchova, moves to 1-1 at FAGE WTA Finals
article_text:
INDIAN WELLS, Calif. -- Just like their past two meetings, Elina Svitolina and Karolina Muchova's second round-robin match at the 2026 FAGE WTA Finals went to a third set.

Wednesday, in their third straight meeting to go to a decider, Svitolina edged Muchova 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 and will have a chance to compete for a semifinal spot in Friday's group stage finale against [2] Aryna Sabalenka. Muchova falls to 0-2 at the competition, and is eliminated from advancing to the semifinals as a result of Mirra Andreeva's win.

With the comeback, she ended Muchova's impressive 32-0 unbeaten record this season after taking the first set -- 26 of those wins had come in straight sets and six in three sets. Svitolina improves to 19-5 in three sets this season, while Muchova dropped just her third deciding set of 17 this year.

"It was important just to try to find my game," Svitolina said. "I was really unhappy with the first set. I tried to put my head down and find the small openings. In the end, I think that the third set was a better level."

Svitolina entered with a 3-1 lead in the head-to-head on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, but the one defeat was their most recent at the Stuttgart semifinals during the clay season. At the time, Svitolina had an unbeaten 6-0 record to Muchova's 7-1 in deciders and Muchova prevailed narrowly in a 6-4, 2-6, 6-4 win. In Miami in 2025, Svitolina earned a 6-2, 3-6, 6-2 victory and has won both hard court meetings between the two.

Muchova is best known for her variety with her shot selection, something that Svitolina pinpointed to when previewing the matchup on Monday.

That variety was present often, with Muchova employing some drops shots, crafty forehands and coming to the net to pressure Svitolina, who was positioned at the baseline. That variety and pressure is how Muchova quickly took the first set.

"She played well the first set," Svitolina added. "Tactically, I didn't execute as well, and she's always a tough player -- she has a good serve, good forehand and slices."

The Ukrainian, in contrast to her opening match, settled into the contest in the second set, adjusting to Muchova's variety and led 4-2 in the second set as the Czech started to commit more errors -- Svitolina's winner to unforced error ratio went from 5:14 in the first set to 12:11 in the second set. Following a Muchova double fault, one her eight on the day, Svitolina closed the second set on her serve, sending their third straight match to go to a decider.

"After that first set, I kind of let her get back into the match," Muchova said. "It was getting tougher and tougher for me, and I lost the rhythm and she gained it."

Svitolina carried that momentum into the third set, winning in similar fashion by a double break, and finished with 22 winners -- 17 of them came in the final two sets. Svitolina, who only dropped four games across the final two sets, has now earned her 11th win at the FAGE WTA Finals and her first since 2019. She's also 6-1 at the WTA Finals in three-set matches.

"I was striking the ball better today in the second and third set than in Stuttgart because in Stuttgart I missed my opportunity and she took over," Svitolina said.

title: Kidambi Srikanth Upsets Kodai Naraoka, Storms Into Kumamoto Masters Quarterfinal

title: Yamaguchi Reflects on 11-Match Losing Streak to An Se-young

Yamaguchi defeated Akechi Hina (Japan) 2-0 (22-20, 21-10) in the first round of the 2026 BWF World Tour Kumamoto Masters (Super 500) held in Kumamoto, Japan, on the 10th.

I’ll strive to deliver a performance true to myself in the next tournament."

title: DP World Tour Championship: Rory McIlroy 'trending well' in pursuit of record-equalling Race to Dubai victory
article_text:
Former Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley believes Race to Dubai victory will boost Rory McIlroy’s ambition to be remembered as the best European golfer of all-time.

McIlroy arrived at the season-ending DP World Tour Championship second in the season-long standings, with the world No 2 looking to win the Race to Dubai for an eighth time and a fifth year in a row.

Winning the Harry Vardon Trophy would see him match Colin Montgomerie's tally of eight Order of Merit titles, with McIlroy making a strong start by posting an opening-round 69 at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

McIlroy moved within two shots of early leader Joost Luiten and three strokes clear of Eugenio Chacarra, the player ahead of him in the rankings, with McGinley expecting the Northern Irishman to keep pushing forward and contend for more Dubai success.

"When he's got a finishing point in mind and a goal that he really wants to achieve, he generally delivers," McGinley told Sky Sports. "This means a lot to him to surpass Monty [Colin Montgomerie].

"I think he's going to be right here until the end. Whether he gets over the line or not, we don't know - golf is not that predictable, but I like where he's at. I think he's trending well and he was the outstanding player of the leading players today [first round].

"We talk about his game evolving, but I think his mind has evolved as well too. It's very hard to go out and put in the 101 per cent effort week in, week out with all the other stuff that he's got going on in his life.

"What you're seeing now is a McIlroy who's picking his battles. Obviously winning majors is a big part of that and he's getting better at that, with two Masters in the last two years, and we're starting to see this Order of Merit become more important to him.

"I don't think we're going to see him maybe back to the world No 1 again, because that takes two years of consistency and that's not where he's at the moment - he's more concerned with other battles that are more important to him.

"He wants to be the outstanding, unquestionable best European player of all time and he's certainly on the way to that. Winning more Order of Merits than everybody else is a big part of that, on top of winning majors."

Nine players entered the week with a mathematical chance of winning the Race to Dubai, but Chacarra, McIlroy and Patrick Reed were the only three who could potentially move to No 1 without winning the season finale.

Reed made an over-par start as Casey Jarvis, Jayden Schaper, Aaron Rai and Ryan Fox - all requiring a victory and results to go their way - also failed to break bar, seeing their slip Race to Dubai hopes fade.

"Some guys have taken themselves out of the equation in terms of the Race to Dubai, but I think this tournament is open," McGinley added. "McIlroy looked particularly good, but Chacarra is not going to roll over easily!

"I think it's three-horse race - Rahm's still a factor and I thought, coming into this week, that McIlroy, Chacarra and Rahm were the three with the best chance.

"Patrick Reed came out of the blocks really early and got a lot of ranking points at the start of the season, but he's gone off form in the last couple of months and it's no surprise to see him drifting away.

"A few guys have come to the party this year that McIlroy might not have had in previous years. It's not as straightforward to win the Race to Dubai as it might have been in previous years - McIlroy knows he's in a battle."

McIlroy claimed his maiden Order of Merit in 2012 before winning back-to-back titles from 2014, with the now 37-year-old proud of his longevity.

"I've never lost my enthusiasm for the game," McIlroy said after his opening round. "This game can beat you down at times and make you quite cynical - I've never let it get to me like that.

"I've seen some others throughout the years, where it has gotten to them a little bit. I've always tried to be grateful that I get to play this game for a living.

"I think that gratitude and that enthusiasm to go to the golf course and compete every day, I've never lost that. Hopefully I never will lose that until I decide to hang 'em up."

title: Panathinaikos strike record stadium rights agreement with Novibet
article_text:
Greek soccer giants Panathinaikos FC have announced a record sponsorship agreement with domestic sportsbook Novibet for the naming rights to its new home stadium.

Sportcal understands the deal is worth an initial €50 million ($55.6 million) across a seven-year term, with bonuses (likely related to domestic performance) taking the figure to a maximum of €53 million.

The value makes the deal the most valuable sports sponsorship agreement in Greece.

The annual fee of €7-7.5 million eclipses local rival (and reigning Greek champions) AEK Athens’ naming rights deal with rival betting operator Allwyn, which is reportedly worth less than a third of Novibet’s sponsorship, around €2 million per year.

Per GlobalData Sport, that figure places the Novibet sponsorship in the top 15 stadium sponsorship agreements in Europe, in a similar range to Groupama’s sponsorship of French side Olympique Lyonnais’ home, or Turkish brand TUPRAS’ naming rights for the stadium of Istanbul giants Besiktas.

Earlier in the year, Allwyn’s attempt to acquire Novibet was scrapped after the Hellenic Competition Commission, the country’s competition authority, intervened.

Had the deal gone through, this sponsorship may not have taken place in the same fashion, if at all.

The name of the new 39,074-capacity venue, set for completion ahead of the 2027-28 campaign, has not yet been confirmed, although it is likely to have two separate monikers, a Novibet-branded official name, and an unbranded cultural name to link it to Panathinaikos.

Unlike many other stadium naming rights deals, Novibet is not an existing partner of Panathinaikos, and will not extend its partnership beyond the stadium, meaning that rival operator Superbet, which holds the front-of-shirt inventory for Panathinaikos’ first team, will retain that branding slot.

Through the first 10 games of the 2026-27 campaign, Panathinaikos sits atop the Greek Super League with 27 points, putting them on track to win a first league title since the 2009-10 season.

title: New chair for NZC; Lord’s ties up with Gullivers Sports Travel
article_text:
The New Zealand Cricket (NZC) governing body has a new chair, with Kevin Malloy having been elected into that role today.

Malloy, current chair of the Super Rugby Pacific organization, succeeds Diana Puketapu-Lyndon, who has now stepped down from the NZC board after completing the maximum nine years as a director.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

He has been an NZC director since 2019, and has also served as deputy chair of the body.

Outside of cricket, meanwhile, Malloy has spent 29 years at worldwide media agency Starcom, working in London, Hong Kong, and New York. He rose to eventually become chief executive of international operations there.

He commented, following his election, which took place after the NZC's annual general meeting: "It is an honour to be asked to lead NZC as chair, and it’s a responsibility I take on with a strong understanding of how much the game means to so many New Zealanders.

"The landscape of cricket is evolving rapidly, both here and around the world, and while that brings challenges, it also brings opportunities.

"We know we are competing for attention against a myriad of other sports and entertainment products, so it’s upon us as an organisation to ensure Kiwis continue connecting with and loving cricket."

New Zealand is preparing to co-host the ICC Men's T20 World Cup in 2028, and is also laying the foundations to launch its own franchise Twenty20 league – the NZ20 – at the end of 2027.

The men's team is currently hosting India in a lucrative series for NZC, meanwhile.

The AGM saw the NZC 2025-26 accounts adopted – the governing body lost NZ$7.3 million during the last financial year, a loss of close to four times that which was originally predicted.

For the 2026-27 financial year, however, NZC is forecasting a budget surplus of over NZ$10 million, with the always-lucrative tour by India's men's team expected to swell the organization's coffers.

Mid-October saw NZC tie up two major commercial agreements as the tour by India got underway. Indian brands Hero MotoCorp and Ai+ Smartphone are both now sponsoring that series.

Puketapu-Lyndon, meanwhile, joined the NZC in 2017, before being elected chair in November 2023 – becoming the first woman to head up the organization, as she replaced Martin Snedden.

The AGM also saw Raewyn Lovett and Jono Brent elected to the NZC board for the first time – both have previously chaired sporting bodies and organizations in New Zealand.

Elsewhere in cricket, the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) – the organization that owns the iconic Lord's Cricket Ground in London – has partnered up with Gullivers Sports Travel.

That firm, which provides sports-based travel and tour packages and has a host of sporting partnerships in place, now becomes the first official short breaks partner of Lord's.

Gullivers, through this multi-year deal, will sell matchday tickets to major events at Lord's – including international fixtures and games from English domestic cricket's The Hundred – alongside accommodation packages.

Packages include tickets to the Lord's Test match next year between England and Australia, with this quadrennial 'Ashes' fixture always an iconic occasion.

Andy Muggleton, the MCC's commercial director, commented: "We are continuing to open up Lord’s to new audiences in innovative ways and this is another first for us. It is an exciting opportunity for cricket supporters who want the full experience of visiting London to watch cricket at Lord’s, combined with the specialist travel support of a trusted operator like Gullivers.”

title: P&O Ferries to transport Tour de France teams for 2027 Grand Départ
article_text:
P&O Ferries has signed as ferry transport partner of the Grand Départ Grande-Bretagne 2027, taking teams, media, partners, vehicles and equipment between the UK and mainland Europe for the Tour de France and Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift.

The operator will use its Dover–Calais and Hull–Rotterdam routes to move the race convoy for both events. It runs more than 300 sailings a week across nine ports in the UK and Europe.

The 114th Tour de France starts in Edinburgh on 2nd July 2027, with stages through England and Wales taking in Carlisle, Liverpool and Cardiff. It will be the third time the UK has hosted the start of the men’s race, after London in 2007 and Yorkshire in 2014. The sixth Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift starts in Leeds on 30th July 2027 and covers 1,156km over nine stages. It will be the first time both races have started in the same country outside France.

The deal follows British Cycling’s appointment of Pitch Marketing Group earlier this week as lead creative agency for the Grands Départs. The organisers say the event will be the largest free-to-spectate sporting event in UK history.

P&O Ferries has been investing in its Dover–Calais service, bringing in two hybrid, double-ended ships, P&O Pioneer and P&O Liberté. They can sail in either direction without turning in port, and are designed to cut fuel consumption and carbon emissions by 40% compared with the vessels they replaced.

Kasper Moos, CEO at P&O Ferries, said, “We are incredibly proud to be named the Official Ferry Transport Partner of the Grand Départ Grande Bretagne 2027. The Tour de France holds a special place in sporting history, and being part of its return to the UK is a real source of pride for everyone at P&O Ferries.“

“Connecting the UK and Europe is at the heart of what we do, and we’re delighted to play our part in bringing this landmark event together.”

Christian Prudhomme, Director of the Tour de France, said, “One of the great strengths of the Tour de France and Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift lies in their ability to connect with the public, wherever they may be. Organising events on such a scale requires reliable and experienced partners.“

“Thanks to its network and operational expertise, P&O Ferries will play a key role in the organisation of the event, ensuring the transport of teams, media, partners, vehicles and equipment between the United Kingdom and France. We are delighted to welcome P&O Ferries as the Official Ferry Transport Partner of the Grand Départ Grande-Bretagne 2027 of the Tour de France.”

title: McNabney set for debut as Irish make seven changes
article_text:
Ulster's James McNabney is poised to make his Ireland debut off the bench as head coach Andy Farrell makes seven changes for Saturday's Nations Championship match against Fiji.

In addition to a raft of personnel changes, Farrell has made two key positional switches with Nick Timoney and Mack Hansen moving to number eight and full-back.

Timoney's switch comes amid an injury crisis at number eight, with Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Sean Jansen all ruled out through injury, while Hansen replaces Hugo Keenan, who drops out of the squad after scoring a hat-trick of tries in the 42-12 win over Argentina.

Jamie Osborne, Bundee Aki, Tommy O'Brien and Jamison Gibson-Park are also drafted into the backline, with Rob Baloucoune and Sam Prendergast retained.

In the pack, Ronan Kelleher starts at hooker with Dan Sheehan ruled out because of concussion, while James Ryan partners stand-in captain Tadhg Beirne in the second row as Joe McCarthy drops out.

With Timoney switching to number eight, former World Rugby player of the year Josh van der Flier is recalled at open-side flanker.

Were McNabney to be called upon, it would cap a remarkable ascent for the 23-year-old, who has started just one game for Ulster this season after recovering from the anterior cruciate ligament injury that forced him to miss the entire 2025-26 campaign.

McNabney is one of four Ulster players on the bench alongside hooker Tom Stewart, prop Tom O'Toole and centre McCloskey, who drops out of the starting line-up for the first time in 2026.

With back-to-back world champions South Africa bringing their much-vaunted scrum power to Dublin next week, Farrell has opted to stick with first-choice props Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong.

Behind an experienced second row of Ryan and Beirne, Ryan Baird keeps his place at blind-side flanker after impressing on his return against Argentina, while Timoney is entrusted with a first Test start at number eight after an eye-catching showing at open-side last week.

Back-up lock Darragh Murray is in line to win his fourth cap off the bench.

With Keenan not included, Hansen returns to the full-back jersey. The 28-year-old scored a hat-trick of tries on his first start at 15 against Australia last year.

Tommy O'Brien returns to left wing while Aki - a late withdrawal from the Argentina game because of illness - and Osborne represent a new centre partnership.

Gibson-Park returns at scrum-half after Craig Casey was preferred last week, while Prendergast is retained at fly-half with Ciaran Frawley kept in reserve.

Ireland sit third behind France and England in the Nations Championship northern hemisphere standings with three wins from four games.

Fiji, who have never beaten Ireland, lost 54-17 to France last week and sit bottom of the southern hemisphere table having failed to win a point.

Head coach Jake White has retained only six starters from the defeat in Lyon, with 31-year-old centre Setareki Bituniyata handed a debut.

title: Aryna Sabalenka explodes on court at WTA Finals as she is hammered by Mirra Andreeva
article_text:
Aryna Sabalenka was handed a tennis lesson by Mirra Andreeva at the WTA Finals and she lost her cool long before the end of a one-sided contest.

Sabalenka appeared to be taking control as she exploded out of the blocks quickly, but a remarkable run of points saw Andreeva win 20 of the last 23 points to clinch the first set.

Andreeva then won 11 of the first 13 points of the second set to take total control of the match and she recorded a 6-4, 6-0 win to book her place in the semi-finals in Indian Wells.

“That was a shocker for Sabelenka,” declared Sky Sports commentator Jonathan Overend. “This was a thrashing. I don’t know how Sabelenka recovers from this.

The final analysis confirmed world No 3 Andreeva needed only one hour and two minutes to dismantle Sabalenka, with world No 2 Sabalenka winning just 31 per-cent of her second serve points.

Incredibly, Sabalenka won just 28 of the 85 points played in the match and she lost 11 games in succession to crash to defear, with Andreeva surprised by the ease of her victory.

“She was playing very good in the beginning,” said Andreeva. “She is a big hitter and likes to go for her shots. She is definitely one of the most aggressive players on tour, so I had to find my rhythm.

“After the first four or five games, I was finding my game and I am just so happy I did what I had to do until the very end.

“I feel like Aryna didn’t have her best day on court as she doesn’t normally make so many mistakes on a normal day. So I feel like I cannot take all the credit for today.”

Andreeva’s modest assessment of the match should not disguise that this was a sparkling performance from the 19-year-old.

While Sabalenka was not at her best and appeared to be struggling with a knee problem, she was also comprehensively outclassed by her young rival.

Sabalenka was rushing through games long before the end of the match as she appeared to lose faith in her ability to compete with Andreeva.

She also let out cries of despair on several occasions and constantly glanced to her box as he looked for inspiration as the wheels came off her game.

In an interview with reporters after losing to Andreeva, Sabalenka was asked what she would say to herself if she were her coach.

Sabalenka replied: “What a f***ing loser (laughs)!

“Uh, no, [I would say]: ‘just keep going, you’re doing okay. If things didn’t go well today, it doesn’t mean that tomorrow is gonna be the same.’

“And I’m a hard worker, and I know that I can push through, whatever.

“I have to say that she played great tennis; that’s for sure and I was just struggling with my rhythm.

“The good news is that I still have my chance to qualify for the semis, so let’s see.”

The defeat leaves Sabalenka with a tough task to try and recover her form and confidence for a final group stage match against Elina Svitolina, where a win will see her qualify for the semi-finals.

title: BHP Mitsubishi Alliance Extends Queensland Firebirds Partnership Through 2028
article_text:
BHP Mitsubishi Alliance (BMA) and Netball Queensland have executed a two-year commercial partnership extension, locking in support through to 2028.

Under the renewed contract, BMA retains its standing as an Official Partner of Netball Queensland and the SSN’s Queensland Firebirds, while maintaining its position as Foundation Partner of the Queensland Firebirds Academy.

The partnership focuses heavily on expanding high-performance regional pathways, enabling young athletes, coaches, and umpires across regional Queensland to access elite netball infrastructure without relocating to metropolitan centers.

“We’re really proud of what this partnership has achieved over the past two years, particularly the opportunities it has created for young people and communities across regional Queensland.”

“Extending our partnership with Netball Queensland and the Queensland Firebirds gives us the opportunity to build on that success and continue supporting netball participation and development pathways across the regions.

“For us, it’s about creating opportunities for young athletes and using sport to bring communities together and connect them with the Queensland Firebirds,” Lancey said.

title: Major Wales star released from squad and replaced with immediate effect
article_text:
Wales tighthead prop Tomas Francis has been ruled out of the remainder of the Nations Championship, after picking up a knee injury in training.

The 34-year-old had been expected to start against New Zealand this week, but will now play no further part in the autumn - having been released back to his club, Sale Sharks. Cardiff prop Keiron Assiratti has been called up as a replacement.

Bath prop Archie Griffin, fresh from his first Test try, keeps his place in the starting team to face New Zealand, with Dragons tighthead Dillon Lewis providing cover on the bench. You can see the full Wales team and follow Steve Tandy's press conference here.

Earlier this week, Francis - who returned to Test rugby earlier this year after a two-and-a-half year absence - spoke about reaching a fourth World Cup.

"You never think far ahead and I was happy to get one cap then," said Francis about making his first global tournament in 2015.

"You just keep trying to improve and stay in that competition for the jersey.

"So now a [fourth World Cup], is a great carrot to have."

Having been given the summer off as he returned from France to head back to the Gallagher Prem, Francis had been brought back into the fold by Tandy.

"The rugby's been good, there's some world-class players there," said Francis this week.

"The environment's a bit different to the second division in France in that respect, but I've enjoyed it.

"The results haven't gone for us yet, but it's a new team.

"There are exciting youngsters there and they've also brought in some old heads. Hopefully we can kick on when we click."

Francis isn't the only injury blow Wales have suffered this week.

No. 8 Aaron Wainwright has been ruled out with a calf injury, although it isn't expected to keep him out for the rest of the autumn campaign.

Earlier this week, Dan Lydiate described the Leicester back-row wearing a protective boot as "precautionary".

It has handed Taine Basham his first Wales start in over four years.

“I’m delighted that Taine gets an opportunity this weekend," said Tandy. "It’s been a while since his last appearance for Wales but he didn’t give up and has put in a lot of dedication and hard work to get back.

"The way he’s been playing for Cardiff has been great and I’m excited to see him go on Saturday.”

title: Lucy Shuker: British wheelchair tennis player retires after 24-year career
article_text:
British wheelchair tennis player Lucy Shuker has retired after 24 years as a professional and three Paralympic medals.

The 46-year-old represented GB at five consecutive Paralympics and won one silver medal and two bronze between 2012 and 2020, in the women's doubles alongside Jordanne Whiley.

A nine-time Grand Slam finalist and seven-time World Team Cup medalist, Shuker announced during Wimbledon this year that she would retire at the end of the season.

At the time she had 98 doubles titles and achieved her aim of reaching 100 earlier this month, when she and Ruby Bishop won at the WC50 Abingdon in Oxfordshire. Shuker also won 39 singles titles.

She was awarded the British Empire Medal for services to sport in 2023 and was GB's flagbearer for the opening ceremony of the 2024 Paralympics in Paris.

"I would like to congratulate Lucy on her fantastic career and thank her for the contribution she has made to wheelchair tennis both on and off the court," said the LTA's chief executive Scott Lloyd.

"To compete at the highest level of the game for over 20 years is a remarkable achievement and testament to her dedication and professionalism.

"She has been, and will continue to be, a passionate advocate for the development of the sport and we look forward to working with her to continue to grow the game for future generations."

Her last match came on Wednesday at the Wheelchair Tennis Finals in Barcelona, where she and Ksenia Chasteau were beaten 6-3 6-1 by the Dutch pair of Diede de Groot and Aniek Van Koot.

Shuker lived and trained in Somerset for much of her career, spending most of it ranked just outside the world's top 10. She retires ranked 23rd in the world, the British number two behind Cornelia Oosthuizen (20).

title: ATP partnership revenues rise 49% to record high
article_text:
ATP has delivered its strongest partnership performance to date, with central partnership revenues rising 49% year on year in 2026.

The increase sees ATP central partnership revenues surpass the $100 million mark for the first time. Since 2022, revenues have increased by more than 200%, driven by new agreements and expanded investment from longstanding partners such as Emirates, Infosys, Nitto, Lexus, Haier and Yokohama, some of which have worked with ATP for more than a decade.

This year’s growth was fuelled by new partnerships with EQT and K-Swiss, alongside continued investment from existing partners. Earlier this week, ATP also announced a multi-year partnership with Julius Baer, which becomes ATP’s first Official Wealth Management Partner and the first Official Partner of the ATP Coaches Programme, with activation across five ATP tournaments on three continents from 2027.

The performance reflects growing demand from brands seeking to connect with tennis fans around the world through ATP’s global reach. It also reflects the continued evolution of the ATP Tour under OneVision, with investment in premium events, enhanced fan experiences and greater collaboration across the sport helping create new commercial opportunities.

Improved tournament infrastructure and growing audiences across ATP’s digital and social platforms have increased the value of partnering with the Tour, while ATP can now better report on the reach and impact of its partnerships. ATP’s global footprint also enables brands to scale partnerships across multiple markets and tailor activations to specific regions and audiences. Collaboration with ATP’s Athlete Marketing team has given partners new ways to engage fans through authentic player-led content and storytelling.

Growth has also been driven by the launch of a dedicated Licensing & Retail team within ATP’s central business division in 2025, which has strengthened ATP’s brand equity and opened the door to new licensing agreements. ATP’s new partnership with K-Swiss, for example, includes the creation of a collection of five ATP-branded tennis shoes, sold globally through K-Swiss, as well as through ATP’s online and in-person retail stores.

Daniele Sano, ATP Chief Business Officer, said: “Since 2022, we have more than tripled our partnership revenues through a combination of new agreements and increased investment from longstanding partners. This success is providing benefits across the Tour. Many of our central partnerships include on-site rights at ATP tournaments, and more than 70% of partnership revenues are paid to tournaments for the rights and activation they provide to our partners. Our new partnership with Julius Baer adds further momentum and we remain confident in our outlook as we target a further double-digit increase in partnership revenues in 2027.”

The benefits are being felt across the sport, with a quarter of a billion dollars invested in the sport through tournaments and players since 2022. ATP projects further double-digit growth in 2027.

title: World No. 1 Seo Seung-jae and Kim Won-ho Eliminated in Round of 16 After Losing to World No. 116 Jin Yong and Cho Song-hyun
article_text:
World No. 1 men's doubles badminton pair Seo Seung-jae and Kim Won-ho were eliminated in the round of 16 at the Kumamoto Masters after losing to fellow South Koreans Jin Yong and Cho Song-hyun, ranked 116th in the world.

Seo and Kim lost 2-0 to Jin and Cho in the men's doubles round of 16 at the Badminton World Federation (BWF) World Tour Super 500 Kumamoto Masters held in Kumamoto, Japan, today (November 12).

In the first game, Seo and Kim kept the score close but conceded two consecutive points from 19-19, losing 21-19.

In the second game as well, they lost control after giving up six straight points from a 9-9 tie.

They later narrowed the gap to two points at 15-13, but ultimately lost 21-15 after conceding three points in a row.

title: Brutal New Slow-Play Rules Coming For 2027 With LPGA Tour ‘Heading In The Wrong Direction’
article_text:
Despite plenty of penalties being handed out for slow play, the LPGA Tour was actually getting slower this year according to its data - so the tour has introduced even tougher sanctions to speed things up in 2027.

Timing data for the year showed penalties increased, the number of timed holes went up 12 percent and although overall the pace of play flatlined, the average time of twosomes in tournament play actually increased by seven minutes.

"The data told us we were heading in the wrong direction," LPGA player president Vicki Goetz-Ackerman said in a memo to players on Tuesday at The Annika in Florida.

The Pace of Play Committee unveiled tougher new sanctions for 2027 including the removal of warnings, stricter time limits and increased fines - all of which were welcomed by World No.1 Nelly Korda and others including Charley Hull.

"I’m a big fan," Korda said. "Anything to get the game a little faster for us players, for fans, for everyone, I think they’re doing a really good job.

"I mean, at the end of the day, no one wants to be out here for five-plus hours. No player wants to. Nobody wants to watch it. I think we’re just moving in the right direction."

Hull, one of the quickest players on Tour, added: "I think it's good. Anything that is going to be harsh I think is good.

"I'm happy about that. Hopefully we can play in four hours now. It literally took me an hour and 40 to play in the Pro-Am today. Like that's great. I wish we did that on Tour."

Pace of play is a huge topic in pro golf, and especially on the LPGA Tour, so after seeing the stats the tour has decided to go even further to avoid things getting out of hand.

In 2027, there's no warnings before players are fined for taking too long over their shots, so anyone taking up to five seconds longer now gets a $2,000 for a first offence, $4,000 for the second and $8,000 on a third.

Taking between 6-15 seconds too long sees players handed a one-shot penalty and a fine, while 16+ seconds over will result in two shots gone and a fine.

There's a crackdown on repeat offenders too with anyone getting timed on 35 holes (down from 40) during the season given a hefty $35,000 fine - and additional fines of $1,000 a hole until 40 and $2,000 thereafter.

And to underpin all of this, the excessive shot time limit has been cut by 10 seconds down to a flat one minute.

"Pace of play matters to our players, our fans and our partners, and we committed to reviewing our policy every year to make sure it’s working," an LPGA spokesperson told Golf.com.

"After a close look at this season’s data and conversations with our players, we’re strengthening the policy for 2027 with tighter time limits and stronger, earlier consequences for players who exceed them.

"Going forward, we’ll keep measuring, keep listening to our players and keep adjusting as we work to further improve pace of play."

The LPGA will hope that players soon get the message to quicken up and avoid slow play becoming a serious issue again.

title: Patrick Reed eyes top finish in Race to Dubai with 2027 PGA Tour card on the line at DP World Tour Championship
article_text:
Patrick Reed nearly aces No. 3, sets up birdie at Genesis Scottish Open

The DP World Tour Championship kicks off in Dubai, with heavy implications for the top-10 finishers who are not already exempt on the PGA Tour.

Reed sits No. 3 in the Race to Dubai Rankings after winning the Dubai Desert Classic and the Qatar Masters earlier this year. His consistent play throughout the year has put him in position to become just the second American to win the Race to Dubai.

“To have to finish in the top 10 to earn my spot on the PGA Tour, and basically come out and believe in myself and put all my eggs in one basket and go get the job done means a lot,” Reed said Tuesday. “We have one more week, and still have that opportunity to be the second American to win the Race to Dubai, which would mean a lot to me. So hopefully we can go out there and cap off the year.”

Patrick Reed's 163-yard approach sets up birdie on No. 4 at Genesis Scottish Open

Reed spent more than a decade on Tour, pairing nine victories with a fiery competitive edge that made him a fixture on Ryder Cup and Presidents Cup teams. Reed's pathway back to the U.S. Team has been difficult to envision. Limited opportunities to earn Official World Golf Ranking points caused him to slide down the rankings, while his absence from Tour competition left him out of Ryder Cup conversation.

A 2027 PGA Tour card could vault Reed back into the conversation regarding international team events.

“Any time I can represent the United States and wear red, white and blue means a lot for me," Reed said. "And I know obviously for my team and my family, and yeah, to get back and playing on those Ryder Cup teams and being a thorn in the side for those Europeans has always been something I've always enjoyed and had fun with."

The timing of Reed's potential return is notable. U.S. Ryder Cup Captain Jim Furyk recently shifted Ryder Cup qualification to a single-year points cycle, replacing the previous two-year accumulation period.

This means that the playing field is even for all players, and a great year for Reed could quickly move him back into contention for a trip to Adare Manor, the site of the 2027 Ryder Cup.

Patrick Reed gets up-and-down from 46 yards for birdie on No. 12 at Genesis Scottish Open

Reed could also be a much-needed spark for the United States, as the U.S. Team hopes to end its Ryder Cup losing streak at two following a 13-15 loss against Team Europe at Bethpage Black in 2025, the first home loss for the U.S. Team since 2012.

Across three Ryder Cup appearances, Reed compiled a 7-3-2 record and became known for his emotional match-play performances, particularly during the 2016 matches at Hazeltine, where his Sunday singles duel with Rory McIlroy helped define the event.

“I know next year it's going to be important to go out there and play really well next year to make the team,” Reed said in Dubai. “It's definitely going to be a part of the goals, if not right there, right at the top of first things I want to do, is go out there and represent our country and play for the USA.”

While a 2027 PGA Tour card wouldn't guarantee Reed a return to Ryder Cup competition, it would remove the biggest obstacle standing in the way of his fourth Ryder Cup appearance. Reed arrives in Dubai with an opportunity to accomplish two significant goals in the same week: become the second American to win the Race to Dubai and put himself on a path back to the biggest stages in golf.

title: DP World Tour golfer slams "worst greens we've had in a long time" at $10m season finale
article_text:
Bernd Wiesberger criticised the condition of the greens at the DP World Tour Championship after enduring a frustrating opening round at Jumeirah Golf Estates.

The Austrian struggled to find his rhythm on Thursday, carding a 3-over 75 to sit 41st in the 50-man field after the first 18 holes.

Dutchman Joost Luiten leads the way, with Masters champion Rory McIlroy firmly in contention to claim a record-equalling eighth Harry Vardon Trophy.

Wiesberger may not be in contention to win the Race to Dubai, but he still has plenty to play for as he looks to secure one of the 10 PGA Tour cards on offer, world ranking points and prize money.

The former European Ryder Cup player made three birdies but saw those gains wiped out by four bogeys and a double bogey.

His biggest setback came at the par-4 9th, where he found himself in the middle of the fairway but went on to three-putt from around 30 feet.

After signing for his 75, Wiesberger took to social media to share his frustration.

Posting on his Instagram story, the 41-year-old wrote: "Average golf + tricky conditions + worst greens on tour we have had in a long time = 75. Onwards to tomorrow to try and get a few back."

Wiesberger also shared a video of playing partner Tyrrell Hatton, who experienced his own difficult moment on the greens during the opening round.

Hatton missed a short putt for par and was left in a state of disbelief.

The incident occurred on the 14th hole, where Hatton was left visibly stunned after missing from around three feet.

Sharing the footage, Wiesberger described it as "quite definitely the highlight of the day", adding a series of laughing emojis.

Hatton, who is renowned for wearing his heart on his sleeve, appeared equally bemused by the miss, pointing towards the hole before looking towards Wiesberger and his caddie, Hugo Dobson.

Despite the moment of frustration, the Englishman enjoyed a considerably better opening day than his playing partner.

The world number 23 carded a two-under-par 70 to finish inside the top half of the leaderboard.

title: Euroleague extends Panini tie-up; FeedConstruct and DBBL partner

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

title: NIFL renews ticketing partnership with TicketCo
article_text:

title: Jake White swings axe: Fiji superstar's return 1 of 9 changes for Ireland clash
article_text:
Fiji have rung the changes ahead of Saturday’s Nations Championship clash with Ireland, making nine alterations to the side that were beaten 54-17 by France in Lyon.

New head coach Jake White has retained just six starters from that defeat, with the most notable call seeing back-row powerhouse Peceli Yato handed the captaincy. The former Clermont star only returned to the international fold this year after a three-year absence and will lead the side from No.8 at the Aviva Stadium.

There is also a fairytale storyline of sorts in midfield after 31-year-old Setareki Bituniyata is handed a Test debut.

The former French Pro D2 Player of the Season comes straight into the starting XV and will partner returning superstar Josua Tuisova in the centres. It will be 113 kg centre’s first Test outing since facing Scotland in July.

The changes continue up front too. Peni Ravai replaces Saracens’ Eroni Mawi at loosehead prop while Joseva Tamani comes into the second row. Mesake Vocevoce, who started in the engine room against France, shifts to blindside flanker as White reshuffle the pack.

Yato is joined in the back row by Lekima Tagitagivalu, while former England international Nathan Hughes misses out after suffering an injury on his Fiji debut last weekend.

In the backs, veteran playmaker Ben Volavola is recalled at fly-half and links up with Frank Lomani in a new-look half-back combination. Ponipate Loganimasi replaces the injured Salesi Rayasi at full-back, while dangerous wings Selestino Ravutaumada and Jiuta Wainiqolo are retained.

title: Elina Svitolina makes ‘angry’ confession after keeping WTA Finals hopes alive with comeback win
article_text:
Elina Svitolina has revealed she used anger to fuel her crucial comeback victory over Karolina Muchova at the 2026 WTA Finals.

World No 6 Svitolina prevailed 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 against seventh-ranked Muchova in her second match in Group 2 at the season-ending championships on Wednesday.

Svitolina’s victory kept her hopes of qualifying for the semi-finals in Indian Wells alive after her 0-4, 0-6 loss to Mirra Andreeva in her opening match.

Muchova, who was beaten 7-6(2), 7-5 by Aryna Sabalenka in her first match, has been eliminated from semi-final contention.

Andreeva secured her progress from the round robin stage as the winner of Group 2 after hammering Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 in her second match.

The winner of the third round robin match between Svitolina and Sabalenka on Friday will join Andreeva in the last four.

In an interview with the WTA after defeating Muchova, Svitolina said: “Yeah, really proud of the effort.

“It was not an easy match for me. She played really well on the first set. I tried to find some openings in the second, but really happy I could stay, could fight and find my good level in the third.

“I tried just to find a better level. I think some opportunities that I missed in the first set just made the difference.

“Then in the second, I tried just to put my head down and fight and just serve better, play better from the baseline.

“She’s a very tricky player. She plays with lots of variety, so you need to find some opportunities in a rally.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, Svitolina explained she was “angry” at herself following her defeat to Andreeva, and after losing the first set against Muchova.

“I was pretty angry at myself, to be fair, after the first match and after the first set, also,” said the 32-year-old Ukrainian.

“Things didn’t go my way, so I tried to direct this anger towards the ball and found my game in the end.

“I played good. I think the level was back in the third set. I just tried to give it all in this match because I know I would be eliminated if I lost.

“So I just tried to really release all this energy and find, you know, these openings against Karolina. She’s such a tough opponent.

“It’s the last tournament of the season, so I just have to really put my head down and deal with all the small injuries.

“I mean, it’s normal that everyone is tired. Everyone is struggling with something here and there.

“I will just try to do my best, have an ice bath and try to heal as much as possible in like 48 hours.”

title: Canada and USA Enter High Performance Agreement
article_text:
Rugby Canada and USA Rugby have launched a four-year high-performance pathway agreement to unify player development and lock in a recurring annual calendar of cross-border competition. Rather than treating one another solely as fierce regional rivals, the two governing bodies are combining resources to build a shared ecosystem of senior test matches, joint training camps, and age-grade tournaments. This alliance establishes a predictable, long-term foundation designed to elevate North American rugby on the world stage over the next decade.

The four-year high-performance pathway agreement between USA Rugby and Rugby Canada builds upon one of North America’s longest-running sporting rivalries. Dating back to the first men’s test match in 1977 and the historic first women’s test outside of Europe in 1987, the two nations have frequently clashed across regional tournaments like the Churchill Cup, the Americas Rugby Championship, and the Pacific Nations Cup. While cross-border youth tours and joint developmental programming were a regular staple of North American rugby prior to 2020, those collaborative pathways were largely neglected in the post-COVID era. As a result, the rival unions often relied on sporadic, ad-hoc fixtures rather than a unified approach to player progression.

Recognizing the need for proactive change to stay competitive on the global stage, both unions formally locked in a fixed, recurring annual calendar in November 2026. Instead of operating in isolation or facing inconsistent scheduling gaps, USA Rugby and Rugby Canada have committed to shared hosting and guaranteed annual test fixtures on both sides of the border for their senior men’s and women’s 15s and sevens programs. This strategic shift ensures that both nations have reliable, high-level international competition every year while aligning their coaching standards and high-performance environments.

A central pillar of this revitalized partnership is the structured expansion of the age-grade pathway, specifically targeting the Men’s U19 and U20 programs alongside the Women’s U20 and U21 squads. By establishing annual cross-border matches and collaborative training camps at these transitional youth levels, the unions are creating a clear, continuous developmental bridge between high school or collegiate rugby and the senior national teams. Growing these U20-level formats gives emerging North American talent consistent exposure to international-style physicality and tactical systems early in their careers, preventing the drop-off in player development that previously hindered both countries.

In the immediate term, this structured four-year cycle serves as a critical launchpad with a direct eye toward the expanded 24-team Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 in Australia. Both the USA Eagles and Canada have qualified for the tournament, which kicks off in October 2027, and the guaranteed slate of cross-border test matches and aligned training camps provides vital preparation time to sharpen their senior rosters and test emerging U20 graduates against familiar, physical opposition.

Looking further ahead, the partnership is explicitly designed as a long-term investment for when the global spotlight turns to North America, with the United States set to host the Men’s Rugby World Cup in 2031 and the Women’s Rugby World Cup in 2033. The current U19, U20, and U21 athletes entering this joint developmental system represent the exact generation of players who will form the core of both national teams during those home-continent tournaments. By fostering a stronger, more competitive North American rugby ecosystem today, USA Rugby and Rugby Canada aim to ensure that both nations arrive at the 2031 and 2033 World Cups capable of delivering historic performances in front of domestic audiences.

title: Steve Tandy makes surprising decision as Wales star left out for All Blacks clash
article_text:
Steve Tandy has made a surprising selection call ahead of Wales’ clash with New Zealand, leaving out one of the team’s most in-form players.

The All Blacks travel to Cardiff following an impressive 43-21 victory over Scotland in Edinburgh, maintaining their unbeaten record in the inaugural Nations Championship.

Wales, meanwhile, head into the fixture on the back of a win over Japan. They will be desperate to end their 73-year wait for a victory against New Zealand, having last beaten the All Blacks in 1953.

However, Tandy has named his matchday squad without Rhys Carre, despite the loosehead prop establishing himself as one of Wales’ most important players in recent times.

The Saracens forward started all three of Wales’ Nations Championship fixtures during the summer before coming off the bench in last weekend’s victory over Japan.

He also featured in four Six Nations matches earlier this year, scoring three tries. One of those was a stunning effort against Ireland, which went on to win Try of the Tournament.

Carre made his professional debut for Cardiff in 2016 before moving to Saracens three years later.

The 28-year-old has since earned more than 30 Wales caps, featured at the 2019 Rugby World Cup and returned to the international fold in 2025 after missing out on selection for the 2023 tournament.

But he has now found himself on the outside looking in once again, with Tandy opting to leave him out of the 23 entirely for Saturday’s showdown.

Nicky Smith has been named at loosehead, with Gareth Thomas providing cover from the bench. Tandy has also confirmed that Carre’s absence is purely down to selection rather than an injury concern.

Given his recent performances and importance to the Welsh pack, the decision is likely to raise eyebrows, particularly with the prop enjoying a strong run of form.

Carre was previously overlooked under Warren Gatland, and it appears he is now facing a similar situation under his successor.

title: NBC Golf Announcer Dan Hicks Dies Aged 64
article_text:
Legendary sports broadcaster Dan Hicks, one of the most well-known voices in golf, has died at the age of 64.

The NBC Golf play-by-play announcer had been in his role since 2000 and commentated on a vast number of iconic moments within the sport such as Tiger Woods' famous 2008 US Open triumph and JJ Spun's 64-foot monster putt at Oakmont in 2025.

Hannah Storm, Hicks' wife and fellow announcer, confirmed his death in a statement on Thursday.

Storm shared that Hicks had been suffering with an "acute illness" but his passing was "sudden" and unexpected. He is survived by his wife and three children.

She said: "Our family is heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected passing of Dan following an acute illness.

"He was a devoted husband of over 30 years, loving father to our three daughters, and cherished friend to so many. His loss is immeasurable.

“Dan was truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around.

Subscribe to the Golf Monthly newsletter to stay up to date with all the latest tour news, equipment news, reviews, head-to-heads and buyer’s guides from our team of experienced experts.

"When he walked into a room, he brought the energy, the laughter and the people together.

"He was endlessly kind, thoughtful and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered.

“Our three daughters and I are heartbroken. We are grateful for the love and support surrounding our family during this incredibly difficult time. These are simply no words to express how much he will be missed.”

Hicks began his career at CNN in 1989 before moving to NBC in 1992. There, he worked as a tower golf announcer prior to earning his big break at the turn of the millennium.

In the 26 years which followed, Hicks was the prevailing voice for NBC at the US Open as well as The Open Championship, the Ryder Cup, the Presidents Cup and Players Championship.

Outside of golf, Hicks called swimming and skiing at the Olympics as well as a number of Notre Dame football games.

A statement from NBC Sports’ Rick Cordella, Sam Flood and Molly Solomon read: “Dan Hicks was an extraordinary colleague, friend and person. In his 34 years at NBC Sports, he was an exceptional storyteller and caller of games and events who elevated some of the biggest moments in sports history.

“From Olympic swimming and skiing to Notre Dame Football, numerous other high-profile events and especially as the signature voice of our golf coverage for the last 26 years, Dan’s blend of knowledge style, enthusiasm and humor informed and entertained fans for decades.

"But far beyond his on-air excellence, Dan was a better person who welcomed teammates with a smile, a joke, or a word of encouragement, sometimes all three in the same sentence.

"Our heartfelt condolences and love to his wife Hannah and his daughters Hannah, Ellery and Riley.”

Meanwhile, multiple other personalities or entities in the golfing world paid tribute to one of the finest voices in the game.

The PGA Tour said: “We are devastated by the sudden loss of Dan Hicks. For more than 25 years leading NBC golf coverage, Dan’s voice filled our living rooms with his steady narration of countless golf broadcasts, calling some of the game’s biggest moments.

“The sound of his voice is woven into our memories of the game, and the warmth he brought to the broadcast was matched only by the kindness he showed those around him.

"Our hearts are with Dan’s family, his wife Hannah, and friends, and with our family at NBC Sports.

"On behalf of everyone at the PGA Tour, we share their sorrow as we mourn someone who meant so much to this game.”

Meanwhile, Golf Channel's Rich Lerner said on a broadcast: “In this job, you hear the news, whatever it is, and you’re supposed to write. But in this case, for a long time, nothing hit the page.

"I couldn’t formulate the words, would not commit to the phrase, the permanence of it all: Dan Hicks is gone. It simply does not make sense. Dan was 64 going on 44.”

Colt Knost posted his tribute on X, which read: "So sad to hear about the passing of Dan Hicks.

"I grew up listening to him and always loved his passion for sports. Was lucky enough to spend some time around him the last several years and you will not find a nicer man! He will be missed."

title: Kota Kaneko named 2026 Sir Henry Cotton Rookie of the Year
article_text:
Kota Kaneko has been named the Sir Henry Cotton Rookie of the Year for 2026, becoming the second Japanese player to win the DP World Tour’s prestigious award.

Kaneko lit up his debut season with a two-week stretch in May as he finished runner-up at the Soudal Open and won the Austrian Alpine Open presented by Kitzbühel Tirol seven days later.

He recorded a further four top 20 finishes to qualify as one of the leading 50 available players in the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World competing in the season-ending DP World Tour Championship.

The 24-year-old continues the success of Japanese players on the DP World Tour in recent years, with Ryo Hisatsune becoming the first player from Japan to win the Sir Henry Cotton Rookie of the Year award in 2023. With his victory this season, Kaneko became one of five Japanese players who have claimed six titles since 2023.

“First of all, I'm very honoured to receive the award,” said Kaneko. “The first person was Ryo Hisatsune, which is a good friend of mine, he’s the same age, and I know him really well. So, I'm really happy to be in the same category with him.

“I think the level of play in Japan has gotten better, and a lot of the players want to go overseas to play. I think that helps a lot of players coming out here and playing really well.

“I was really happy winning in Austria, and that gave me big confidence that I knew I could play out here. And from here on, just coming out at the end of the season, playing the two DP World Tour tournaments was kind of one of the goals. So I'm happy to be here.

“I work really hard by taking every tournament step by step in every shot. And worked really hard, and I think this got me to where I am right now.”

Kaneko won twice on the Japan Golf Tour in 2025 to top the Order of Merit and earn an exemption on the DP World Tour for the 2026 season.

He recorded a T15 finish in the second event of his DP World Tour career at the Qatar Masters in February. He enjoyed a further top 20 followed by his first top ten of the season in back-to-back appearances at the Volvo China Open and Turkish Airlines Open, before his successful two-week run in Belgium and Austria yielded his maiden victory.

Kaneko earned the Sir Henry Cotton Rookie of the Year award by finishing as the leading eligible player on the Race to Dubai Rankings Delivered by DP World. He entered the DP World Tour Championship in 49th position, and as the only contender for the award competing in the season-ending event in Dubai.

Guy Kinnings, Chief Executive Officer of the DP World Tour, said: “On behalf of everyone at the DP World Tour, I’m delighted to congratulate Kota on becoming the 2026 Sir Henry Cotton Rookie of the Year.

“With his victory in Austria, and some impressive performances throughout the year, Kota certainly made an impression in his rookie campaign, putting together a string of results that took him all the way to the season-ending DP World Tour Championship.

“His win in May was the first of two for Japanese players on the 2026 Race to Dubai and continued a truly impressive run of success for Japan on the DP World Tour in recent years – perfectly demonstrating the benefits of the partnerships and pathways we have built with Tours around the world.

“We all wish Kota well for the future and look forward to seeing him build on this successful first season.”

title: Shorts: Sportradar, Charlton Athletic Community Trust, Swansea City
article_text:
Sportradar has added DATA.BET, Esportsbull and GRID to its Unified Odds Feed, giving betting operators a choice of esports odds providers through a single integration.

Operators will be able to choose their preferred provider title by title, subject to availability and commercial terms. At launch, the feed covers Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2 and League of Legends. VALORANT and Mobile Legends: Bang Bang are planned next, with more titles and markets to follow.

The expansion is part of Sportradar’s investment in its esports betting business as operator demand grows. Its esports portfolio also includes Match Tracker and audio-visual products for operators.

Each of the three launch providers brings a different specialism. DATA.BET is a sportsbook technology supplier established in 2017. Esportsbull is an esports-only odds and trading business. GRID, founded in 2018, is an official esports data platform that works with publishers and tournament organisers, including Riot Games, Ubisoft, KRAFTON, ESL FACEIT Group and BLAST.

Founded in 2001 and listed on NASDAQ, Sportradar covers more than a million events a year for clients including Flutter, DraftKings, Google and Microsoft, and works with sports organisations including UEFA, FIFA and the Bundesliga.

Roman Garin, SVP, Innovation at Sportradar, said, “Esports’ fully digital nature creates an expectation for fast, deep live betting experiences. The providers that have built the market across Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2 and League of Legends each bring their own strengths and trading style, and the best fit can differ from title to title. By bringing them together through our Unified Odds Feed, we’re giving operators greater choice and flexibility through a single integration, and we’ll continue adding providers and titles as the market evolves.”

Sportradar is also a sponsor of the SIAs, having partnered on the Tech in Sport category in 2026 and will do so again in 2027.

Charlton Athletic Community Trust (CACT) and the London Borough of Bexley have signed a Memorandum of Understanding formalising a partnership that dates back more than 30 years. The agreement commits the three organisations to joint work on community safety, health, education and employment across the borough.

The agreement was signed at half-time during Charlton’s 2-1 Championship win over Sheffield United at The Valley on 7th November.

It sets out shared priorities for the council, club and trust: reducing anti-social behaviour and youth crime, increasing participation in sport and physical activity, and improving school attendance and attainment. It also covers helping young people into employment, education and training, and strengthening community cohesion. A Bexley and Charlton Steering Group, made up of representatives from key local organisations and sectors, will oversee the partnership, share best practice and identify future funding.

CACT already works with thousands of residents across south-east London, running programmes for children, young people, families, schools and vulnerable groups. Its relationship with the council began in 1993, when Bexley jointly funded the trust’s first Community Officer. The club’s Schools Partnership Scheme works with more than 30 primary schools in the borough.

The agreement is one of the first public commitments from Ben Mansford since he became Charlton’s Chief Executive Officer last month.

Ben Mansford, Chief Executive Officer of Charlton Athletic, said, “Working closely with Charlton Athletic Community Trust and Bexley Council is central to our commitment to making a positive and lasting difference across the communities we serve. Through our Schools Partnership Scheme, we engage with more than 30 primary schools across Bexley, providing young people with opportunities to attend matches, meet players and raise valuable funds for their schools.

“We are also incredibly proud of the impact Charlton Athletic Community Trust delivers every day. As a club, we look forward to continuing to support its work alongside Bexley Council, helping to create opportunities, inspire young people and improve lives across the borough.”

Jason Morgan, Chief Executive Officer of Charlton Athletic Community Trust, said, “I have had the privilege of working alongside Bexley Council for more than 30 years, and I have seen first-hand the positive impact that strong partnerships can have on local communities. Our relationship dates back to 1993 when the council jointly funded our very first Community Officer, laying the foundations for a collaboration that has continued to grow and evolve over three decades.

Councillor David Leaf, Leader of Bexley Council, said, “This agreement reflects our shared commitment to improving the lives of Bexley residents and helping to continue to make it a great place to live, work and raise a family. We have a longstanding and successful relationship with the Charlton Athletic Community Trust and the impressive work they do in our community has changed the lives of residents and young people. I have seen first-hand the enjoyment they bring when getting people active and the encouragement, support and safe places they provide to help young people in need of some encouragement, mentoring and support.

“By working even more closely with the club and CACT, we can build on existing successes and create more opportunities for local people to be active, healthy and connected to their communities.”

Swansea City has extended its partnership with The Turmeric Co., the recovery drinks brand founded by former Wales international Hal Robson-Kanu, for the 2026/27 season. It will be the sixth consecutive season of the deal.

As the club’s turmeric partner, The Turmeric Co. supplies its products to Swansea City’s men’s teams. The partnership began in 2021, and the products are now part of the Championship club’s performance and recovery programme.

title: Pumas lose 324 caps' worth of experience from starting XV for Italy
article_text:
Argentina will be without 324 caps’ worth of experience from the starting XV that faced Ireland when they take on Italy in Genoa on Saturday.

Felipe Contepomi has made five changes following the 42-12 defeat in Dublin, with Julián Montoya, Marcos Kremer and Juan Cruz Mallía all ruled out through injury, while Juan Martín González and Gonzalo García drop to the bench.

Montoya’s absence accounts for 120 of those lost caps after the hooker suffered a head injury against Ireland. Bautista Bernasconi, who has just three caps, will make his first Test start in his place.

Kremer, an 83-cap veteran, misses out with a sprained right ankle, prompting another reshuffle in the back-row. Pablo Matera moves from No.8 to blindside and captains Argentina for the fourth time in five Tests, with eight-cap Joaquín Moro and three-cap Juan Martín Scelzo completing the loose trio.

González’s 51 caps are moved to the bench, while 19-cap García is replaced at scrum-half by Simón Benítez Cruz.

Mallía’s injury removes another 51 caps from the run-on side. Bautista Delguy consequently shifts to full-back, allowing Rodrigo Isgró to start on the wing.

Facundo Bosch and Facundo Isa return among the replacements, with Isa in line for his first Test appearance since July 2025.

Leonel Oviedo has also left the squad after suffering a knee injury, while Benjamín Grondona has been called in following Kremer’s setback.

Argentina XV: 15 Bautista Delguy, 14 Rodrigo Isgró, 13 Justo Piccardo, 12 Santiago Chocobares, 11 Mateo Carreras, 10 Tomás Albornoz, 9 Simón Benítez Cruz; 1 Boris Wenger, 2 Bautista Bernasconi, 3 Francisco Moreno, 4 Guido Petti, 5 Pedro Rubiolo, 6 Pablo Matera (c), 7 Joaquín Moro, 8 Juan Martín Scelzo.

Replacements: 16 Facundo Bosch, 17 Mayco Vivas, 18 Joel Sclavi, 19 Ephraim Elias, 20 Juan Martín González, 21 Facundo Isa, 22 Gonzalo García, 23 Gerónimo Prisciantelli.

title: Paralympic medallist Shuker ends 24-year tennis career
article_text:
British wheelchair tennis player Lucy Shuker has retired after 24 years as a professional and three Paralympic medals.

The 46-year-old represented GB at five consecutive Paralympics and won one silver medal and two bronze between 2012 and 2020, in the women's doubles alongside Jordanne Whiley.

A nine-time Grand Slam finalist and seven-time World Team Cup medalist, Shuker announced during Wimbledon this year that she would retire at the end of the season.

At the time she had 98 doubles titles and achieved her aim of reaching 100 earlier this month, when she and Ruby Bishop won at the WC50 Abingdon in Oxfordshire. Shuker also won 39 singles titles.

She was awarded the British Empire Medal for services to sport in 2023 and was GB's flagbearer for the opening ceremony of the 2024 Paralympics in Paris.

"I would like to congratulate Lucy on her fantastic career and thank her for the contribution she has made to wheelchair tennis both on and off the court," said the LTA's chief executive Scott Lloyd.

"To compete at the highest level of the game for over 20 years is a remarkable achievement and testament to her dedication and professionalism.

"She has been, and will continue to be, a passionate advocate for the development of the sport and we look forward to working with her to continue to grow the game for future generations."

Her last match came on Wednesday at the Wheelchair Tennis Finals in Barcelona, where she and Ksenia Chasteau were beaten 6-3 6-1 by the Dutch pair of Diede de Groot and Aniek Van Koot.

Shuker lived and trained in Somerset for much of her career, spending most of it ranked just outside the world's top 10. She retires ranked 23rd in the world, the British number two behind Cornelia Oosthuizen (20).

title: Navy Blue Sports Strengthens PR & Communications Team with Two Appointments
article_text:
Sports marketing and communications agency Navy Blue Sports has strengthened its PR & Communications division by appointing Niamh Ferguson as Senior Account Manager and Rachel O’Brien as Junior Account Executive.

The two appointments add a blend of senior experience across sponsorship, brand strategy and integrated marketing alongside emerging expertise in digital communications and campaign analytics.

Ferguson joins Navy Blue Sports with more than eight years of experience working across sport, sponsorship and brand marketing.

Most recently, she held senior marketing and sponsorship roles with Golf Ireland and Glanbia Performance Nutrition, where she developed and delivered brand and sponsorship strategy for Optimum Nutrition in Ireland.

During her time with Glanbia, she led partnerships with the IRFU, Leinster Rugby and the GAA/GPA, and worked across a portfolio of elite athlete relationships.

She previously spent four years with AIB as Marketing and Content Manager, leading digital content initiatives and supporting the activation of some of the bank’s major sporting partnerships.

Across those roles, Ferguson has built experience spanning PR and media relations, campaign delivery, sponsorship activation, brand development and agency management.

O’Brien joins the agency as Junior Account Executive after completing an MSc in Digital Marketing at UCD Smurfit Graduate Business School. She previously graduated with a first-class honours degree in Sport and Exercise Management.

Her background combines an interest in sport with developing expertise across digital marketing, social media strategy, paid advertising and campaign analytics.

Her postgraduate studies included practical experience using platforms such as Meta Ads Manager and Google Analytics, while work as a Communications and Social Media Volunteer provided hands-on experience in content planning and publishing.

She has also worked as a Brand Ambassador, developing further experience in brand representation and consumer engagement.

The appointments come as Navy Blue Sports continues to build its PR and communications capability within the wider sports marketing agency, bringing together experienced sponsorship and communications expertise with a new generation of digital marketing talent.

title: Lewis Moody's son follows in World Cup-winning father's footsteps with England debut
article_text:
England Rugby World Cup winner Lewis Moody has another reason to celebrate after his 18-year-old son Dylan made his competitive England Under-19 debut in a 4-1 victory over Slovenia.

The 6ft 5in Southampton goalkeeper started between the posts as the Young Lions opened their latest European Under-19 Championship qualifying campaign with an impressive win on Wednesday.

Dylan helped England to victory, with Reigan Heskey scoring twice in a comfortable afternoon for Ben Futcher's side.

It seems sporting success runs in the Moody blood, with Dylan now writing his own chapter in the family history more than two decades after his father helped England lift the Rugby World Cup in 2003.

Lewis Moody earned 71 England caps during a glittering rugby career with Leicester Tigers and Bath.

Nicknamed 'Mad Dog', he was part of Sir Clive Woodward's legendary 2003 World Cup-winning squad.

Now his son is representing England in football.

Dylan joined Southampton's academy aged eight and signed his first professional contract in July 2025.

The teenager has already trained with Southampton's first team and continues to impress at international level.

His latest appearance is another step forward in a promising career.

The family's sporting success comes during a difficult period.

Just days after announcing the diagnosis, the former England captain watched Dylan save a penalty against France during an international youth fixture.

The teenager kept a clean sheet in that 1-0 victory, giving his family a special moment during an incredibly challenging time.

Now Dylan has another achievement to celebrate.

According to the FA's official match report, England will next face Belarus on Saturday before meeting Austria on Tuesday.

Lewis experienced the ultimate international triumph in Sydney in 2003.

Twenty-three years later, his son is beginning to build his own England legacy.

- 🌹 71 England caps between 2001 and 2010.

- 🦁 5 British & Irish Lions caps across the 2005 and 2009 tours.

- 🏉 2001 – Made his England debut against Canada.

- 🏆 7 Premiership titles with Leicester Tigers.

- 🌍 2 Heineken Cup titles with Leicester Tigers.

- 🏟️ Leicester Tigers and Bath – The two clubs he represented during his senior career.

- 🧢 England captain – Led his country during the latter stages of his international career.

- 🐕 Mad Dog – His famous nickname, earned through his fearless playing style.

- 🏅 MBE – Awarded following England's 2003 World Cup triumph.

- 📅 2012 – Retired from professional rugby aged 33.
